Measurements and Units.text: The most appropriate instrument for measuring the internal diameter of a test tube is the
options: micrometer screw gauge
vernier calipers
metre rule
measuring cylinder
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: vernier calipers

Measurements and Units.text: A micrometer screw gauge is most appropriate for measuring
options: the length of a classroom
the diameter of a thin wire
the volume of a liquid
the mass of a stone
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: the diameter of a thin wire

Measurements and Units.text: The SI unit of mass is the
options: newton
kilogram
pound
gram-force
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: kilogram

Measurements and Units.text: A simple beam balance operates on the principle of
options: comparing an unknown mass with known standard masses, using the principle of moments
directly measuring weight, with no reference to mass
measuring volume rather than mass
measuring density directly, with no calculation required
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: comparing an unknown mass with known standard masses, using the principle of moments

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following is classified as a fundamental (base) physical quantity?
options: Force
Time
Velocity
Energy
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Time

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following is classified as a derived physical quantity?
options: Length
Mass
Acceleration
Time
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Acceleration

Measurements and Units.text: The dimension of density is
options: [ML⁻³]
[MLT⁻²]
[LT⁻¹]
[ML²T⁻²]
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: [ML⁻³]

Measurements and Units.text: The dimension of pressure is
options: [ML⁻¹T⁻²]
[MLT⁻¹]
[ML²T⁻²]
[LT⁻²]
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: [ML⁻¹T⁻²]

Measurements and Units.text: Dimensional analysis is primarily useful for
options: determining the precise numerical constant in a physical formula
checking whether a physical equation is dimensionally consistent (homogeneous)
directly measuring a physical quantity in the laboratory
calibrating a thermometer’s fixed points
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: checking whether a physical equation is dimensionally consistent (homogeneous)

Measurements and Units.text: The number of significant figures in the value 0.05060 is
Writing 0.000072 in standard form gives
The accuracy of a measurement refers to
options: how many decimal places are recorded
how close the measured value is to the true (actual) value
the specific instrument brand used
the precision of the measuring scale alone, regardless of the true value
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: how close the measured value is to the true (actual) value

Measurements and Units.text: A systematic (zero) error in a measuring instrument is one that
options: varies randomly with each reading taken
consistently shifts every reading in the same direction, often due to a fault such as a mis-set zero
never affects any experimental result
can only occur with electronic, not mechanical, instruments
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: consistently shifts every reading in the same direction, often due to a fault such as a mis-set zero

Measurements and Units.text: Displacement of a body is defined as its
options: total distance travelled, regardless of direction
change of position in a specified direction, measured as the shortest path from start to finish
speed multiplied by the total time taken
mass multiplied by its velocity
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: change of position in a specified direction, measured as the shortest path from start to finish

Measurements and Units.text: Distance differs from displacement mainly because distance is
options: a vector quantity, unlike displacement
a scalar quantity, having magnitude only, unlike displacement which also specifies direction
always smaller in value than displacement
measured only in kilometres, while displacement is measured only in metres
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: a scalar quantity, having magnitude only, unlike displacement which also specifies direction

Measurements and Units.text: The position of a point on a plane surface is commonly specified using
options: a single numerical value only
Cartesian (x, y) coordinates relative to a chosen reference frame
mass and time only
colour and texture
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Cartesian (x, y) coordinates relative to a chosen reference frame

Measurements and Units.text: A eureka can (displacement can), used together with a measuring cylinder, is designed to determine the
options: mass of a solid
volume of an irregularly shaped solid, by liquid displacement
temperature of a liquid
time for an event to occur
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: volume of an irregularly shaped solid, by liquid displacement

Measurements and Units.text: A zero error on a metre rule, where the rule’s edge is slightly worn, would generally cause measurements taken with it to be
options: always identical to the true length
consistently either too long or too short by a fixed amount, unless corrected for
affected only on alternate readings
unaffected in any way
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: consistently either too long or too short by a fixed amount, unless corrected for

Measurements and Units.text: Random errors in an experimental measurement can generally be minimized by
options: taking only a single reading
taking several repeated readings and calculating their average
using a poorly calibrated instrument
ignoring the measurement process altogether
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: taking several repeated readings and calculating their average

Measurements and Units.text: Deriving the unit of a quantity such as pressure (force per unit area) from fundamental units illustrates that
options: pressure is itself a fundamental quantity
pressure’s unit can be built up from the fundamental units of mass, length, and time
pressure has no defined unit
pressure is unrelated to force or area
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: pressure’s unit can be built up from the fundamental units of mass, length, and time

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following correctly lists three of the seven recognized SI fundamental (base) quantities?
options: Force, energy, and power
Length, mass, and time
Velocity, acceleration, and momentum
Density, pressure, and volume
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Length, mass, and time

Measurements and Units.text: A stopwatch is generally used in the laboratory to measure
options: mass
short time intervals, such as the period of a swinging pendulum
length
temperature
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: short time intervals, such as the period of a swinging pendulum

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following is an example of a derived SI unit?
options: The second
The kilogram
The newton (kg m s⁻²)
The metre
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: The newton (kg m s⁻²)

Measurements and Units.text: Testing whether a given physics equation is dimensionally correct involves checking that
options: both sides give the same numerical answer
both sides of the equation have identical dimensions
the equation contains only fundamental quantities
the equation involves no derived quantities whatsoever
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: both sides of the equation have identical dimensions

Measurements and Units.text: Expressing very large or very small measured quantities in standard (scientific) notation is useful mainly because it
options: makes numbers appear artificially larger
simplifies representation, calculation, and clearly conveys the number of significant figures
removes the need to state any units
applies only to whole numbers
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: simplifies representation, calculation, and clearly conveys the number of significant figures

Measurements and Units.text: The volume of an irregularly shaped stone can be determined experimentally using
options: a metre rule alone
the liquid displacement method with a measuring cylinder or eureka can
a stopwatch
a thermometer
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: the liquid displacement method with a measuring cylinder or eureka can

Measurements and Units.text: A frame of reference in physics is best described as
options: a coordinate system relative to which the motion or position of a body is described
a type of measuring instrument used only for mass
a fixed unit of time
a quantity unrelated to position or motion
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: a coordinate system relative to which the motion or position of a body is described

Measurements and Units.text: The dimension of velocity, [LT⁻¹], can be derived from the fundamental quantities of
options: mass and time only
length and time
mass and length only
mass, length, and time combined in a different way
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: length and time

Measurements and Units.text: A vernier caliper’s “vernier scale” allows for
options: measurement to a coarser precision than a plain metre rule
more precise measurement (finer than the main scale alone) by reading the position where a vernier division aligns with a main scale division
no improvement in measurement precision at all
measurement of temperature rather than length
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: more precise measurement (finer than the main scale alone) by reading the position where a vernier division aligns with a main scale division

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following correctly explains why estimating the possible experimental error in a measurement is considered good laboratory practice?
options: It has no bearing on how the result should be interpreted
It provides an indication of how much confidence can reasonably be placed in the measured or calculated result
Experimental error can always be assumed to be zero if care is taken
Only theoretical physics, not laboratory practice, requires error estimation
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: It provides an indication of how much confidence can reasonably be placed in the measured or calculated result

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following correctly describes why repeated timing of a single oscillation of a simple pendulum is generally less accurate than timing a larger number (e.g., 20) of oscillations and dividing by that number?
options: Timing a single oscillation always gives a more accurate period than timing many oscillations
Timing many oscillations spreads any fixed reaction-time error over a larger total time, reducing its proportional effect on the calculated period of a single oscillation
The number of oscillations timed has no bearing on the accuracy of the calculated period
Reaction-time errors only affect single-oscillation timing, never multiple-oscillation timing
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Timing many oscillations spreads any fixed reaction-time error over a larger total time, reducing its proportional effect on the calculated period of a single oscillation

Measurements and Units.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of accurate measurement and appropriate choice of instrument in physics practical work?
options: Selecting an instrument appropriate to the required precision, and understanding potential sources of error, underpins the reliability of all subsequent experimental analysis and conclusions
Instrument choice has no bearing on the reliability of experimental results
Any instrument may be used interchangeably for any measurement, regardless of required precision
Error estimation and instrument selection are relevant only to advanced research, not standard school practicals
Measurements and Units.correct_answer: Selecting an instrument appropriate to the required precision, and understanding potential sources of error, underpins the reliability of all subsequent experimental analysis and conclusions

Scalars and Vectors.text: A scalar quantity is completely specified by
options: magnitude and direction
magnitude alone
direction alone
neither magnitude nor direction
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: magnitude alone

Scalars and Vectors.text: A vector quantity requires, for complete specification, both
options: magnitude and direction
magnitude alone
two magnitudes
neither magnitude nor direction
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: magnitude and direction

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
options: Weight
Displacement
Energy
Momentum
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: Energy

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
options: Mass
Speed
Acceleration
Time
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: Acceleration

Scalars and Vectors.text: Speed and velocity are distinguished by the fact that
options: speed specifies direction, unlike velocity
velocity specifies direction, while speed (its magnitude equivalent) does not
they are identical quantities in every respect
neither quantity has a defined magnitude
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: velocity specifies direction, while speed (its magnitude equivalent) does not

Scalars and Vectors.text: Two forces acting in the same straight line and direction on a body are combined by
options: subtracting the smaller from the larger
simply adding their magnitudes
multiplying their magnitudes
finding the square root of the product of their magnitudes
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: simply adding their magnitudes

Scalars and Vectors.text: Two forces of unequal magnitude acting in exactly opposite directions along the same line are combined by
options: adding their magnitudes
subtracting the smaller magnitude from the larger, with the resultant acting in the direction of the larger
multiplying their magnitudes
the resultant is always zero, regardless of the magnitudes
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: subtracting the smaller magnitude from the larger, with the resultant acting in the direction of the larger

Scalars and Vectors.text: The parallelogram law is used to determine the resultant of
options: a single vector acting alone
two vectors acting at an angle to one another
only scalar quantities
only vectors acting in exactly the same direction
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: two vectors acting at an angle to one another

Scalars and Vectors.text: Resolving a single force into two mutually perpendicular components allows
options: the force to be entirely eliminated from further analysis
each perpendicular direction to be analysed independently, simplifying calculations involving forces acting at an angle
the force’s direction to be permanently reversed
the force to be treated purely as a scalar quantity
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: each perpendicular direction to be analysed independently, simplifying calculations involving forces acting at an angle

Scalars and Vectors.text: If a force F acts at angle θ above the horizontal, its horizontal component is given by
options: F sin θ
F cos θ
F tan θ
F
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: F cos θ

Scalars and Vectors.text: If a force F acts at angle θ above the horizontal, its vertical component is given by
options: F cos θ
F sin θ
F tan θ
F
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: F sin θ

Scalars and Vectors.text: Relative velocity describes the
options: velocity of a body as measured from a fixed, universal frame of reference only
velocity of one moving body as observed from another moving (or stationary) reference body
velocity of a body that is permanently at rest
sum total of all velocities in the universe
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: velocity of one moving body as observed from another moving (or stationary) reference body

Scalars and Vectors.text: A graphical (scale-drawing) method of vector addition involves
options: drawing the vectors to scale, joined tail-to-head, with the resultant measured directly from the completed diagram
using no diagram whatsoever, relying only on mental calculation
treating all vectors as if they were scalar quantities
ignoring the direction of each vector entirely
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: drawing the vectors to scale, joined tail-to-head, with the resultant measured directly from the completed diagram

Scalars and Vectors.text: Two perpendicular vectors of magnitude 6 units and 8 units combine to give a resultant of magnitude
options: 14 units
10 units
2 units
48 units
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: 10 units

Scalars and Vectors.text: The direction of a resultant vector formed from two perpendicular component vectors can be found using
options: simple addition of the component magnitudes alone
an appropriate trigonometric ratio, such as the inverse tangent of the ratio of the components
multiplying the two component magnitudes together
the direction cannot be determined from the components
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: an appropriate trigonometric ratio, such as the inverse tangent of the ratio of the components

Scalars and Vectors.text: According to the triangle law of vector addition, if two vectors are represented as two sides of a triangle, taken in order, the resultant is represented by
options: the sum of the two sides’ lengths, in the same direction as either original vector
the third side of the triangle, taken in the opposite sense to the first two
a vector always equal to zero
a line perpendicular to both original vectors
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: the third side of the triangle, taken in the opposite sense to the first two

Scalars and Vectors.text: Weight is properly classified as a vector quantity because it
options: has magnitude only
has both a magnitude and a specific direction (vertically downward, toward the Earth’s centre)
has no defined magnitude at all
is entirely unrelated to the concept of force
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: has both a magnitude and a specific direction (vertically downward, toward the Earth’s centre)

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following is generally treated as a scalar, rather than vector, quantity in elementary mechanics?
options: Momentum
Kinetic energy
Weight
Acceleration
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: Kinetic energy

Scalars and Vectors.text: The equilibrant of a set of forces acting on a body is a single force that
options: has the same magnitude and same direction as their resultant
has the same magnitude as their resultant but acts in the exactly opposite direction, restoring equilibrium
is entirely unrelated to the resultant force
always has zero magnitude
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: has the same magnitude as their resultant but acts in the exactly opposite direction, restoring equilibrium

Scalars and Vectors.text: Resolving forces into components is particularly valuable for analysing situations such as
options: an object on a frictionless inclined plane, where gravity’s effect can be split into components parallel and perpendicular to the slope
a single force acting along a single axis, with no angle involved
situations where direction is never a relevant consideration
purely scalar quantities such as mass or temperature
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: an object on a frictionless inclined plane, where gravity’s effect can be split into components parallel and perpendicular to the slope

Scalars and Vectors.text: A boat crossing a river, whose actual path over the ground is affected by the current, illustrates a practical application of
options: mass conservation
relative velocity, combining the boat’s velocity relative to the water with the water’s velocity relative to the bank
a concept entirely unrelated to vector addition
purely scalar addition of speeds, with no reference to direction
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: relative velocity, combining the boat’s velocity relative to the water with the water’s velocity relative to the bank

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following correctly explains why simply adding the magnitudes of two vectors, without considering direction, generally gives an incorrect resultant unless the vectors are exactly collinear?
options: Vector addition must account for both magnitude and direction, since vectors combine according to their relative orientation, not magnitude alone
Vectors have no direction, making simple magnitude addition always correct
Vector and scalar addition are always identical procedures
Direction is only relevant for scalar quantities, not vectors
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: Vector addition must account for both magnitude and direction, since vectors combine according to their relative orientation, not magnitude alone

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following correctly explains why an aircraft’s actual path over the ground (its “ground track”) can differ from the direction it is pointed (its “heading”), particularly in the presence of wind?
options: The aircraft’s resultant velocity over the ground is the vector sum of its velocity relative to the air (heading direction) and the wind’s velocity, which can differ in direction from the heading alone
Wind has no effect on an aircraft’s actual path over the ground
An aircraft’s ground track is always identical to its heading, regardless of wind
Vector addition has no application to aircraft navigation
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: The aircraft’s resultant velocity over the ground is the vector sum of its velocity relative to the air (heading direction) and the wind’s velocity, which can differ in direction from the heading alone

Scalars and Vectors.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the practical importance of resolving and combining vectors in analysing physical situations such as forces in equilibrium or the motion of projectiles?
options: It allows complex, multi-directional problems to be broken into simpler, independently analysable perpendicular components
Vector resolution and combination have no practical application in physics problem-solving
All physics problems can be fully solved while ignoring the direction of relevant quantities
Vector methods are relevant only to abstract, non-applied theoretical physics
Scalars and Vectors.correct_answer: It allows complex, multi-directional problems to be broken into simpler, independently analysable perpendicular components

Motion.text: Uniform velocity describes motion in which a body covers
options: unequal displacements in equal time intervals
equal displacements in equal time intervals, in a fixed direction
unequal distances only when accelerating
no displacement at all, over any time interval
Motion.correct_answer: equal displacements in equal time intervals, in a fixed direction

Motion.text: Uniform acceleration describes motion in which the velocity of a body
options: remains completely constant
changes by equal amounts in equal time intervals
changes randomly, with no consistent pattern
is always exactly zero
Motion.correct_answer: changes by equal amounts in equal time intervals

Motion.text: Speed is defined as
options: displacement per unit time, in a specified direction
distance covered per unit time, without reference to direction
the rate of change of velocity
identical in every respect to acceleration
Motion.correct_answer: distance covered per unit time, without reference to direction

Motion.text: Velocity is defined as
options: distance covered per unit time, without direction
displacement per unit time, in a specified direction
identical in every respect to speed
the rate of change of displacement squared
Motion.correct_answer: displacement per unit time, in a specified direction

Motion.text: Acceleration is defined as the
options: distance covered per unit time
rate of change of velocity with respect to time
same physical quantity as velocity
total distance covered by a moving body
Motion.correct_answer: rate of change of velocity with respect to time

Motion.text: The equation v = u + at relates final velocity (v) to initial velocity (u), acceleration (a), and
options: displacement (s)
time (t)
mass (m)
force (F)
Motion.correct_answer: time (t)

Motion.text: The equation s = ut + ½at² is used to calculate
options: displacement, given initial velocity, acceleration, and time
only the final velocity of a moving body
only the mass of a moving body
only the force acting on a moving body
Motion.correct_answer: displacement, given initial velocity, acceleration, and time

Motion.text: The equation v² = u² + 2as relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement, without requiring
options: mass
time
initial velocity
acceleration
Motion.correct_answer: time

Motion.text: For a body falling freely under gravity, ignoring air resistance, the acceleration is
options: zero
approximately constant at 9.8 m/s², directed downward
continuously increasing without any limit
dependent on the falling body’s mass
Motion.correct_answer: approximately constant at 9.8 m/s², directed downward

Motion.text: On a distance-time graph for a moving body, the gradient at any given point represents the body’s
options: acceleration at that point
speed at that point
total distance travelled up to that point
mass at that point
Motion.correct_answer: speed at that point

Motion.text: On a velocity-time graph, the gradient at any given point represents the body’s
options: displacement at that point
acceleration at that point
speed at that point
total elapsed time
Motion.correct_answer: acceleration at that point

Motion.text: On a velocity-time graph, the area enclosed between the graph and the time axis, over a given time interval, represents the
options: acceleration during that interval
displacement (or distance) covered during that interval
initial velocity only
final velocity only
Motion.correct_answer: displacement (or distance) covered during that interval

Motion.text: Instantaneous velocity refers to a body’s velocity
options: averaged over the entire duration of its journey
at one specific, particular moment in time
only at the very beginning of its motion
which never actually changes throughout the motion
Motion.correct_answer: at one specific, particular moment in time

Motion.text: In projectile motion, neglecting air resistance, the horizontal component of the projectile’s velocity
options: changes continuously due to gravity’s effect
remains constant throughout the flight, since gravity acts only in the vertical direction
is always exactly zero
increases without limit
Motion.correct_answer: remains constant throughout the flight, since gravity acts only in the vertical direction

Motion.text: In projectile motion, the vertical component of the projectile’s velocity
options: remains constant throughout the flight
changes continuously due to the constant downward acceleration of gravity
is always exactly zero
is entirely unaffected by gravity
Motion.correct_answer: changes continuously due to the constant downward acceleration of gravity

Motion.text: The maximum height attained by a projectile launched at an angle depends chiefly on
options: the horizontal component of its initial velocity alone
the vertical component of its initial velocity and the acceleration due to gravity
the total mass of the projectile alone
the colour or shape of the projectile
Motion.correct_answer: the vertical component of its initial velocity and the acceleration due to gravity

Motion.text: The horizontal range of a projectile, launched from and landing at the same height, is generally maximized (for a given initial speed) at a launch angle of
options: 0 degrees
45 degrees
90 degrees
an angle that has no bearing on the resulting range
Motion.correct_answer: 45 degrees

Motion.text: Newton’s first law of motion states that a body will remain at rest, or continue moving with uniform velocity in a straight line, unless
options: acted upon by a net (resultant) external force
observed by someone
its mass changes to exactly zero
time itself ceases to pass
Motion.correct_answer: acted upon by a net (resultant) external force

Motion.text: Newton’s second law of motion relates the net force acting on a body to
options: its mass and velocity separately, with no combined relationship
the rate of change of its momentum (equivalently, mass multiplied by acceleration, for constant mass)
its displacement alone
the time elapsed alone
Motion.correct_answer: the rate of change of its momentum (equivalently, mass multiplied by acceleration, for constant mass)

Motion.text: Newton’s third law of motion states that for every action (force), there is
options: no corresponding reaction whatsoever
an equal and opposite reaction
a reaction that is always larger in magnitude
a reaction that is always smaller in magnitude
Motion.correct_answer: an equal and opposite reaction

Motion.text: Inertia describes a body’s inherent tendency to
options: spontaneously accelerate, even in the absence of any applied force
resist any change to its existing state of rest or uniform motion
always eventually come to rest, regardless of applied force
continuously increase in mass over time
Motion.correct_answer: resist any change to its existing state of rest or uniform motion

Motion.text: Momentum of a moving body is calculated as the product of its
options: mass and displacement
mass and velocity
force and the time for which it acts
mass and acceleration
Motion.correct_answer: mass and velocity

Motion.text: Impulse delivered to a body is calculated as the product of
options: the applied force and the time interval over which it acts
the body’s mass and its velocity
the body’s mass and its acceleration
the body’s displacement and the time elapsed
Motion.correct_answer: the applied force and the time interval over which it acts

Motion.text: The area enclosed under a force-time graph represents the
options: work done by the force
impulse delivered by the force
the power developed by the force
the momentum the body had before the force was applied
Motion.correct_answer: impulse delivered by the force

Motion.text: The principle of conservation of linear momentum states that, in the absence of any external force, the total momentum of an interacting system
options: always increases over time
remains constant, both before and after any interaction such as a collision
always decreases over time
is always reduced to exactly zero
Motion.correct_answer: remains constant, both before and after any interaction such as a collision

Motion.text: In a perfectly elastic collision between two bodies, both
options: momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
momentum is conserved, but kinetic energy is not necessarily conserved
neither momentum nor kinetic energy is conserved
mass is destroyed, though momentum is conserved
Motion.correct_answer: momentum and kinetic energy are conserved

Motion.text: In a perfectly inelastic collision, the colliding bodies
options: separate completely, retaining all their original kinetic energy
stick together and move as a single combined body after the collision, with kinetic energy generally not conserved
experience no change in momentum whatsoever
always experience a doubling of their combined kinetic energy
Motion.correct_answer: stick together and move as a single combined body after the collision, with kinetic energy generally not conserved

Motion.text: Centripetal force, relevant to circular motion, is directed
options: tangentially along the circular path
toward the centre of the circular path
directly away from the centre of the circular path
in a direction unrelated to the circular path’s centre
Motion.correct_answer: toward the centre of the circular path

Motion.text: In simple harmonic motion, the restoring force (and resulting acceleration) is generally
options: directly proportional to the displacement from the equilibrium position, and always directed toward that position
constant in magnitude and direction throughout the motion
completely unrelated to displacement from equilibrium
directed away from the equilibrium position at all times
Motion.correct_answer: directly proportional to the displacement from the equilibrium position, and always directed toward that position

Motion.text: In simple harmonic motion, the amplitude refers to the
options: time required to complete one full oscillation
maximum displacement from the equilibrium (mean) position
number of complete oscillations occurring per second
velocity of the oscillating body at the equilibrium position
Motion.correct_answer: maximum displacement from the equilibrium (mean) position

Motion.text: The period of a simple pendulum, for small oscillations, depends mainly on
options: the mass of the pendulum bob and the length of the string
the length of the string and the local acceleration due to gravity, but not on the mass of the bob
only the mass of the pendulum bob, with no dependence on string length
the colour of the pendulum bob
Motion.correct_answer: the length of the string and the local acceleration due to gravity, but not on the mass of the bob

Motion.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a body’s momentum, rather than its velocity alone, is the more fundamentally conserved quantity in a collision between two bodies of different mass?
options: Momentum accounts for both the mass and velocity of each body, and the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant regardless of the internal forces exchanged during collision, unlike velocity, which can change independently for bodies of different mass
Velocity, not momentum, is the quantity conserved in any type of collision
Momentum conservation has no relevance to analysing collisions between bodies of differing mass
Only bodies of identical mass can meaningfully exchange momentum during a collision
Motion.correct_answer: Momentum accounts for both the mass and velocity of each body, and the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant regardless of the internal forces exchanged during collision, unlike velocity, which can change independently for bodies of different mass

Gravitational Field.text: Newton’s law of universal gravitation states that the force of attraction between two masses is
options: directly proportional to the product of the masses, and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them
inversely proportional to the product of the masses
unaffected by the distance separating the masses
directly proportional to the square of the distance between them
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: directly proportional to the product of the masses, and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them

Gravitational Field.text: The universal gravitational constant, G, is
options: different for every distinct pair of interacting masses
a fixed constant, with the same value throughout the universe, appearing in Newton’s law of gravitation
numerically identical to the acceleration due to gravity, g
not required at all in gravitational force calculations
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: a fixed constant, with the same value throughout the universe, appearing in Newton’s law of gravitation

Gravitational Field.text: Gravitational field intensity at a point is defined as the
options: work done in moving a unit mass from infinity to that point
gravitational force experienced per unit mass placed at that point
mass of the object generating the gravitational field
distance from the point to the centre of the gravitating body
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: gravitational force experienced per unit mass placed at that point

Gravitational Field.text: A conservative force field, such as the gravitational field, is one in which
options: the work done moving a body between two points depends on the specific path taken
the work done moving a body between two points is independent of the specific path taken
no work can ever be done on any body within the field
the field varies unpredictably with time, regardless of position
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: the work done moving a body between two points is independent of the specific path taken

Gravitational Field.text: The acceleration due to gravity near the Earth’s surface, g, has a commonly used standard value of approximately
options: 9.8 m/s²
1.6 m/s²
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: 9.8 m/s²

Gravitational Field.text: The value of g on the Earth’s surface
options: is exactly identical at every location, with absolutely no variation
varies slightly depending on latitude and altitude
always increases without limit as altitude increases
has no relationship to distance from the Earth’s centre
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: varies slightly depending on latitude and altitude

Gravitational Field.text: Mass differs fundamentally from weight in that mass
options: is a vector quantity dependent on location, unlike weight
is a scalar quantity representing the quantity of matter in a body and remains constant regardless of location, whereas weight is a force that depends on the local gravitational field strength
is identical to weight in every measurable respect
is measured only in newtons, the same unit as weight
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: is a scalar quantity representing the quantity of matter in a body and remains constant regardless of location, whereas weight is a force that depends on the local gravitational field strength

Gravitational Field.text: Weight of a body is generally calculated using the relationship
options: W = m/g
W = mg
W = m + g
W = g/m
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: W = mg

Gravitational Field.text: Escape velocity refers to the minimum speed an object requires to
options: remain in a stable, fixed orbit indefinitely
completely escape a planet’s gravitational pull, without further propulsion
simply reach the summit of a tall structure
come to a complete stop relative to the planet’s surface
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: completely escape a planet’s gravitational pull, without further propulsion

Gravitational Field.text: A geostationary (parking) orbit is one in which a satellite
options: travels much faster than the Earth’s own rotation
has an orbital period exactly matching the Earth’s rotational period, so it appears stationary above a fixed point on the equator
falls back to Earth almost immediately after launch
has no defined orbital period at all
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: has an orbital period exactly matching the Earth’s rotational period, so it appears stationary above a fixed point on the equator

Gravitational Field.text: Astronauts experiencing “weightlessness” while orbiting the Earth do so mainly because
options: gravity is entirely absent at orbital altitude
both the astronaut and the spacecraft are in continuous free-fall together, eliminating the usual contact force that produces the sensation of weight
their mass has been temporarily reduced to zero
the spacecraft’s structure completely blocks all gravitational effects
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: both the astronaut and the spacecraft are in continuous free-fall together, eliminating the usual contact force that produces the sensation of weight

Gravitational Field.text: According to Newton’s law of gravitation, if the distance between two masses is tripled, the gravitational force between them becomes
options: three times as large
one-ninth as large
one-third as large
nine times as large
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: one-ninth as large

Gravitational Field.text: Gravitational potential energy of a body raised to a height h above a reference level is generally given by
options: mgh
½mv²
mg/h
m/(gh)
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: mgh

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why g generally decreases with increasing altitude above the Earth’s surface?
options: Greater altitude means greater distance from the Earth’s centre, reducing gravitational force per unit mass according to the inverse-square relationship
g consistently increases, rather than decreases, with increasing altitude
g has no relationship whatsoever to distance from the Earth’s centre
Altitude has no bearing on gravitational field strength
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Greater altitude means greater distance from the Earth’s centre, reducing gravitational force per unit mass according to the inverse-square relationship

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why g is very slightly different at the poles compared to the equator?
options: The Earth’s slightly flattened, non-spherical shape means locations at the poles are somewhat closer to the Earth’s centre than locations at the equator, affecting local gravitational field strength
g is exactly identical everywhere on Earth, since the Earth is a perfect sphere
Latitude has no possible effect on gravitational field strength
g depends only on longitude, never on latitude
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: The Earth’s slightly flattened, non-spherical shape means locations at the poles are somewhat closer to the Earth’s centre than locations at the equator, affecting local gravitational field strength

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why gravitational potential is conventionally defined as zero at an infinite distance from a gravitating mass, becoming increasingly negative closer to the mass?
options: Since work must be done against the attractive gravitational force to move a mass away toward infinity, potential is defined to increase (become less negative) with increasing distance, reaching zero only at infinity
Gravitational potential has no meaningful defined reference point
Gravitational potential is always a positive quantity, everywhere in space
There is no relationship between gravitational potential and distance from a massive body
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Since work must be done against the attractive gravitational force to move a mass away toward infinity, potential is defined to increase (become less negative) with increasing distance, reaching zero only at infinity

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly relates escape velocity to a planet’s mass and radius?
options: Escape velocity generally increases with the planet’s mass, and decreases as the planet’s radius increases (for fixed mass)
Escape velocity is completely unaffected by a planet’s mass or radius
Escape velocity decreases as a planet’s mass increases
Escape velocity depends solely on radius, with no dependence on mass
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Escape velocity generally increases with the planet’s mass, and decreases as the planet’s radius increases (for fixed mass)

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why geostationary communication satellites are specifically placed in orbit directly above the equator?
options: An orbit exactly matching Earth’s rotational period, and appearing fixed relative to a ground point, is only achievable directly above the equator, given the geometry of the Earth’s rotation and gravitational field
Geostationary satellites can be placed at any latitude, with identical results
Equatorial positioning has no relevance to achieving a geostationary orbit
Geostationary orbits are impossible for any Earth-orbiting satellite
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: An orbit exactly matching Earth’s rotational period, and appearing fixed relative to a ground point, is only achievable directly above the equator, given the geometry of the Earth’s rotation and gravitational field

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a given mass would weigh less on the Moon than on Earth, despite having identical mass in both locations?
options: The Moon has a weaker gravitational field strength than Earth, due to its smaller mass and radius, so the same mass experiences a smaller gravitational force (weight) there
Mass itself changes when an object is transported to the Moon, altering its weight
Weight is identical everywhere in the universe, regardless of local gravitational field strength
Gravitational field strength has no bearing on an object’s weight
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: The Moon has a weaker gravitational field strength than Earth, due to its smaller mass and radius, so the same mass experiences a smaller gravitational force (weight) there

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why work done in moving a mass through a gravitational field between two fixed points is independent of the specific path taken?
options: Since gravity is a conservative force, any additional work expended moving away from the direct path is exactly regained when moving back toward it, making total work path-independent
Gravitational work strongly depends on the exact path chosen between two points
Gravity behaves as a non-conservative force in this context
Path-independence applies only to non-conservative forces, not to gravity
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Since gravity is a conservative force, any additional work expended moving away from the direct path is exactly regained when moving back toward it, making total work path-independent

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains the practical relevance of understanding gravitational fields to launching and maintaining artificial satellites?
options: Correctly applying gravitational principles allows accurate calculation of the velocity and energy needed to achieve a desired stable orbit or to escape Earth’s gravitational field entirely
Gravitational field theory has no practical bearing on satellite launch or orbital calculations
Satellite launches require no consideration of gravitational principles whatsoever
Orbital mechanics is entirely independent of the concept of gravitational field strength
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Correctly applying gravitational principles allows accurate calculation of the velocity and energy needed to achieve a desired stable orbit or to escape Earth’s gravitational field entirely

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why astronauts orbiting Earth, despite being well within Earth’s gravitational field and experiencing substantial gravitational force, still appear to float freely (weightlessness)?
options: Both the astronauts and their spacecraft are continuously falling freely around the Earth together, so there is no supporting contact force to create the usual sensation of weight
There is genuinely no gravitational force acting on astronauts or spacecraft in orbit
Orbiting spacecraft are located entirely beyond the reach of Earth’s gravitational field
Weightlessness experienced in orbit has no connection to the concept of continuous free-fall
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Both the astronauts and their spacecraft are continuously falling freely around the Earth together, so there is no supporting contact force to create the usual sensation of weight

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the value of G (the universal gravitational constant) is extremely small in SI units, making gravitational attraction between ordinary, everyday- sized objects generally imperceptible?
options: The small numerical value of G means that only when at least one of the interacting masses is very large (such as a planet) does the resulting gravitational force become significant enough to notice
G’s small value means gravitational forces between ordinary objects are actually very large and easily noticeable
The numerical value of G has no bearing on the practical magnitude of gravitational forces
Gravitational force between ordinary objects is always identical in magnitude to that involving planetary-scale masses
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: The small numerical value of G means that only when at least one of the interacting masses is very large (such as a planet) does the resulting gravitational force become significant enough to notice

Gravitational Field.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of understanding gravitational fields in physics and space technology?
options: Gravitational field theory underpins the calculation of orbital trajectories, escape velocities, and satellite behaviour, essential for both theoretical understanding and practical space technology
Gravitational field concepts have no meaningful application to space technology or satellite behaviour
Space technology functions entirely independently of any gravitational field principles
Escape velocity and orbital calculations require no reference to gravitational field theory
Gravitational Field.correct_answer: Gravitational field theory underpins the calculation of orbital trajectories, escape velocities, and satellite behaviour, essential for both theoretical understanding and practical space technology

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A body under the action of coplanar forces is in equilibrium when
options: the resultant force and resultant moment about any point are both zero
only the resultant force is zero, regardless of any resultant moment
all the forces involved are equal in magnitude
only a single force acts on the body
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the resultant force and resultant moment about any point are both zero

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The triangle law of forces states that three coplanar forces in equilibrium, acting at a point, can be represented in magnitude and direction by
options: the three sides of a triangle, taken in order
two unrelated, independent line segments
only two of the triangle’s three sides
a single straight line
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the three sides of a triangle, taken in order

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Lami’s theorem applies to
options: any arbitrary number of forces acting on a body
three coplanar, concurrent forces in equilibrium, relating each force to the sine of the angle between the other two
exactly two forces only
forces that are specifically not in equilibrium
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: three coplanar, concurrent forces in equilibrium, relating each force to the sine of the angle between the other two

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The moment of a force about a given point is calculated as
options: the force multiplied by the time for which it acts
the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the point to the force’s line of action
the force divided by the distance from the point
numerically identical to the force itself
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the point to the force’s line of action

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A couple consists of
options: a single isolated force acting on a body
two equal, parallel forces acting in opposite directions along different lines of action, producing a turning effect
two forces of equal magnitude acting along the very same line, in the same direction
forces that must always act through a single common point
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: two equal, parallel forces acting in opposite directions along different lines of action, producing a turning effect

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The principle of moments states that, for a body in rotational equilibrium, the
options: sum of clockwise moments about a given point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about that same point
resultant force must always be greater than zero
mass of the body must be exactly zero
sum of clockwise moments is always greater than the sum of anticlockwise moments
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: sum of clockwise moments about a given point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about that same point

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The centre of gravity of a body is the single point at which
options: the entire weight of the body may be considered to act
the body’s total mass becomes exactly zero
all external forces on the body must necessarily be equal
the body always experiences its maximum possible acceleration
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the entire weight of the body may be considered to act

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A body is said to be in stable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it
options: moves progressively further away from its original position
tends to return to its original position
remains exactly at the newly displaced position, with no tendency to move further
topples over immediately
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: tends to return to its original position

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A body is said to be in unstable equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it
options: tends to return to its original position
tends to move progressively further away from its original position
remains exactly at the displaced position
is completely unaffected by any displacement whatsoever
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: tends to move progressively further away from its original position

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A body is said to be in neutral equilibrium if, when slightly displaced, it
options: returns to its original position
moves progressively further away from its original position
simply remains in its new position, with no tendency to move further or to return
always falls over immediately
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: simply remains in its new position, with no tendency to move further or to return

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A body with a relatively low centre of gravity and a wide base is generally
options: less stable than a body with a high centre of gravity and a narrow base
more stable than a body with a high centre of gravity and a narrow base
equally stable regardless of the height of its centre of gravity or its base width
always in a state of unstable equilibrium
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: more stable than a body with a high centre of gravity and a narrow base

Equilibrium of Forces.text: A metre rule balanced on a knife-edge pivot, with weights hung at various points along its length, is a classic laboratory illustration of
options: Newton’s third law of motion
the principle of moments
the law of conservation of energy
Ohm’s law
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the principle of moments

Equilibrium of Forces.text: The equilibrant of a system of forces has
options: the same magnitude and same direction as their resultant
the same magnitude as their resultant, but acts in the exactly opposite direction
no defined relationship to the resultant whatsoever
always a magnitude of zero
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: the same magnitude as their resultant, but acts in the exactly opposite direction

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a wide-based tripod stand for laboratory apparatus is generally more stable than a stand with a narrower base?
options: A wider base increases the range over which the centre of gravity can shift, before the vertical line through it falls outside the base, causing toppling
Base width has no bearing on the overall stability of a stand
A narrower base is always more stable than a wider one, for identical apparatus
Only the height of the centre of gravity, never the base width, affects stability
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: A wider base increases the range over which the centre of gravity can shift, before the vertical line through it falls outside the base, causing toppling

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a ladder leaning against a smooth wall requires friction at its base with the ground in order to remain in equilibrium?
options: Without sufficient frictional force at the base, there would be an unbalanced horizontal force, preventing the ladder from satisfying the condition of zero net force required for equilibrium
A leaning ladder can achieve equilibrium without any need for friction at its base
Friction has no relevance to whether a leaning ladder remains in equilibrium
Equilibrium of a leaning ladder depends only on the wall’s reaction force, with no contribution from the ground
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: Without sufficient frictional force at the base, there would be an unbalanced horizontal force, preventing the ladder from satisfying the condition of zero net force required for equilibrium

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why racing cars are deliberately designed with a very low centre of gravity?
options: A lower centre of gravity increases stability, reducing the likelihood of the car toppling over during high-speed cornering
Centre of gravity height has no bearing on a vehicle’s cornering stability
A high centre of gravity is generally preferred for improved cornering stability in racing cars
Racing car stability depends only on tyre grip, with no relevance to centre of gravity
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: A lower centre of gravity increases stability, reducing the likelihood of the car toppling over during high-speed cornering

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why engineers apply the principle of moments when designing load-bearing structures such as bridges and cranes?
options: Ensuring clockwise and anticlockwise moments balance appropriately at supporting points is essential to prevent structural toppling or failure under applied loads
The principle of moments has no relevance to structural engineering design
Bridges and cranes require no consideration of turning effects when being designed
Only the total weight supported matters, with no relevance to how moments are distributed
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: Ensuring clockwise and anticlockwise moments balance appropriately at supporting points is essential to prevent structural toppling or failure under applied loads

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a seesaw balances when a heavier person sits closer to the pivot and a lighter person sits further from it?
options: The principle of moments requires that the product of weight and distance from the pivot be equal on both sides for balance, so a smaller weight at a greater distance can balance a larger weight at a smaller distance
A seesaw can only balance if both people are of identical weight, regardless of their distance from the pivot
The principle of moments has no application to a simple seesaw
Distance from the pivot has no bearing on how a seesaw balances
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: The principle of moments requires that the product of weight and distance from the pivot be equal on both sides for balance, so a smaller weight at a greater distance can balance a larger weight at a smaller distance

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why an object is more likely to topple when tilted if it has a relatively tall, narrow shape, compared to a short, wide object of similar mass?
options: A tall, narrow object’s centre of gravity moves outside its base of support more readily upon tilting, due to the combination of higher centre of gravity and narrower base
Object shape and proportions have no bearing on the likelihood of toppling when tilted
Tall, narrow objects always have a lower centre of gravity than short, wide objects
Wider-based objects are always less stable than narrower-based objects, regardless of height
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: A tall, narrow object’s centre of gravity moves outside its base of support more readily upon tilting, due to the combination of higher centre of gravity and narrower base

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly identifies the everyday application of a couple, as understood in the context of equilibrium of forces?
options: Turning a steering wheel using two hands applying equal and opposite forces at different points on the wheel
A couple has no relevant everyday applications
A couple can only be demonstrated using purely theoretical, non-physical examples
Turning a steering wheel with a single hand illustrates the concept of a couple
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: Turning a steering wheel using two hands applying equal and opposite forces at different points on the wheel

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why resolving forces into perpendicular components is a useful technique when analysing the equilibrium of a body subjected to several forces acting at different angles?
options: Considering each perpendicular direction separately allows the overall equilibrium condition to be checked more systematically, since the sum of forces in each independent direction must separately be zero
Resolving forces into components has no practical benefit for equilibrium analysis
Only a single direction ever needs to be considered, regardless of how many forces act at different angles
Equilibrium can always be determined without any reference to the direction of individual forces
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: Considering each perpendicular direction separately allows the overall equilibrium condition to be checked more systematically, since the sum of forces in each independent direction must separately be zero

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding the concept of centre of gravity is important when loading a truck or lorry with cargo?
options: Distributing cargo so the overall centre of gravity remains appropriately low and centred helps maintain vehicle stability, reducing the risk of tipping, particularly when cornering
Cargo distribution and centre of gravity have no bearing on vehicle stability
A higher centre of gravity always improves a loaded vehicle’s stability
Vehicle stability during cornering depends only on speed, with no relevance to cargo distribution
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: Distributing cargo so the overall centre of gravity remains appropriately low and centred helps maintain vehicle stability, reducing the risk of tipping, particularly when cornering

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a bus is more likely to overturn while cornering if it is carrying passengers standing on an upper deck, compared to when all passengers are seated on the lower deck?
options: Passengers on the upper deck raise the overall centre of gravity of the loaded bus, reducing its stability during cornering
Passenger position within the bus has no bearing on its overall stability
Passengers on an upper deck always lower the bus’s centre of gravity
A higher centre of gravity always improves a vehicle’s stability during cornering
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: Passengers on the upper deck raise the overall centre of gravity of the loaded bus, reducing its stability during cornering

Equilibrium of Forces.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of understanding equilibrium of forces, moments, and centre of gravity in mechanics and everyday engineering?
options: These principles are essential for predicting and ensuring the stability of structures, vehicles, and everyday objects under the combined effect of multiple forces
Equilibrium of forces and related concepts have no meaningful application in everyday engineering practice
Structural and vehicle stability can be reliably ensured without any reference to these principles
These concepts apply only to idealized, purely theoretical problems with no real-world relevance
Equilibrium of Forces.correct_answer: These principles are essential for predicting and ensuring the stability of structures, vehicles, and everyday objects under the combined effect of multiple forces

Work, Energy and Power.text: Work done by a force is defined as the product of the force and the
options: time for which it acts
displacement of its point of application, in the direction of the force
mass of the object it acts upon
square of the object’s velocity
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: displacement of its point of application, in the direction of the force

Work, Energy and Power.text: The SI unit of both work and energy is the
options: newton
joule
watt
pascal
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: joule

Work, Energy and Power.text: Power is defined as the
options: total amount of work done, irrespective of time taken
rate at which work is done, or energy is transferred, per unit time
same physical quantity as force
same physical quantity as energy
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: rate at which work is done, or energy is transferred, per unit time

Work, Energy and Power.text: The SI unit of power is the
options: joule
newton
watt
pascal
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: watt

Work, Energy and Power.text: Kinetic energy possessed by a body of mass m moving with velocity v is given by
options: mgh
½mv²
Fd
m/v
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: ½mv²

Work, Energy and Power.text: Gravitational potential energy of a body of mass m raised through height h is given by
options: ½mv²
mgh
Fd
m/(gh)
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: mgh

Work, Energy and Power.text: The principle of conservation of energy states that energy
options: can be created but never destroyed
can be neither created nor destroyed, only converted from one form to another
is always completely lost in any physical process
always increases without limit over time
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: can be neither created nor destroyed, only converted from one form to another

Work, Energy and Power.text: The area enclosed under a force-distance (force-displacement) graph represents the
options: power developed
total work done
momentum of the body
impulse delivered
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: total work done

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly describes a common energy transformation occurring in a hydroelectric power station?
options: Chemical energy is converted directly into nuclear energy
Gravitational potential energy of stored water is converted into kinetic energy, then into electrical energy via a turbine and generator
Electrical energy is converted directly into gravitational potential energy, with no other stages
No meaningful energy transformation occurs in hydroelectric generation
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Gravitational potential energy of stored water is converted into kinetic energy, then into electrical energy via a turbine and generator

Work, Energy and Power.text: A renewable energy source is one that is
options: permanently exhausted after a single use
naturally replenished over a relatively short timescale, such as solar, wind, and hydroelectric power
exclusively derived from fossil fuels
never usable for electricity generation
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: naturally replenished over a relatively short timescale, such as solar, wind, and hydroelectric power

Work, Energy and Power.text: A non-renewable energy source, such as crude oil or coal, is characterized mainly by
options: being replenished naturally almost as quickly as it is consumed
existing in finite reserves that are consumed much faster than they are naturally replaced
never being used as a fuel source
causing absolutely no environmental impact when used
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: existing in finite reserves that are consumed much faster than they are naturally replaced

Work, Energy and Power.text: A key environmental concern associated with the widespread combustion of fossil fuels is
options: a reduction in the greenhouse effect
increased emission of greenhouse gases, contributing to global warming and climate change
complete elimination of air pollution
no meaningful environmental impact of any kind
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: increased emission of greenhouse gases, contributing to global warming and climate change

Work, Energy and Power.text: Hydroelectric power generation typically works by using the
options: combustion of fuel to produce steam that drives a turbine
kinetic energy of falling or flowing water to turn a turbine connected to a generator
direct conversion of solar radiation into electricity, with no water involved
fission of nuclear fuel to generate heat
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: kinetic energy of falling or flowing water to turn a turbine connected to a generator

Work, Energy and Power.text: Nuclear power stations generate electricity primarily by harnessing energy released during
options: ordinary chemical combustion
nuclear fission, in which heavy atomic nuclei split apart, releasing substantial energy
purely mechanical processes with no atomic-level reactions involved
simple evaporation of water
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: nuclear fission, in which heavy atomic nuclei split apart, releasing substantial energy

Work, Energy and Power.text: A solar panel converts
options: heat energy directly into chemical energy
light energy from the sun into electrical energy, via the photovoltaic effect
electrical energy into visible sunlight
mechanical energy directly into sunlight
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: light energy from the sun into electrical energy, via the photovoltaic effect

Work, Energy and Power.text: Energy diversification, as an energy policy strategy, refers to
options: relying exclusively on a single energy source
using a range of different energy sources to improve the reliability and sustainability of overall energy supply
deliberately excluding all renewable energy sources
relying only on non- renewable energy sources
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: using a range of different energy sources to improve the reliability and sustainability of overall energy supply

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the area under a force-distance graph gives the correct value of work done, even when the applied force varies over the distance travelled?
options: Summing (integrating) the varying force over each small increment of distance correctly accounts for the changing force, giving the true total work done, which the area under the graph represents
The area under a force-distance graph has no meaningful relationship to work done when force is not constant
Work done can only ever be calculated when the applied force is constant throughout
A varying applied force always results in exactly zero net work done
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Summing (integrating) the varying force over each small increment of distance correctly accounts for the changing force, giving the true total work done, which the area under the graph represents

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly explains why hydroelectric dams are typically constructed at locations with significant water flow and a substantial elevation drop?
options: Greater water flow and elevation drop increase the available gravitational potential and kinetic energy that can be converted into useful electrical energy
Dam location has no bearing on the amount of electrical energy that can practically be generated
Hydroelectric dams function equally well regardless of water flow rate or elevation drop
Elevation drop is irrelevant to hydroelectric power generation; only water flow rate matters
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Greater water flow and elevation drop increase the available gravitational potential and kinetic energy that can be converted into useful electrical energy

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly explains why solar panels, unlike fossil fuel power stations, produce no direct greenhouse gas emissions during electricity generation?
options: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity via the photovoltaic effect, without any combustion process, unlike fossil fuel power stations which release combustion by-products including greenhouse gases
Solar panels rely on combustion of solar material, similar to fossil fuel power stations
There is no meaningful difference in emissions between solar panels and fossil fuel power stations
Solar panels produce significantly more direct greenhouse gas emissions than fossil fuel power stations
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity via the photovoltaic effect, without any combustion process, unlike fossil fuel power stations which release combustion by-products including greenhouse gases

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly explains the rationale behind promoting energy conservation and efficiency as strategies for addressing energy-related challenges?
options: Using energy more efficiently reduces overall demand, associated costs, and environmental impact, helping address both supply and sustainability concerns
Energy conservation measures have no meaningful effect on demand, cost, or environmental impact
Improved energy efficiency always results in increased overall energy demand
Energy conservation strategies are relevant only to non-renewable energy sources
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Using energy more efficiently reduces overall demand, associated costs, and environmental impact, helping address both supply and sustainability concerns

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding energy sources and their associated environmental impacts is important for national policy-making regarding electricity generation?
options: Well- informed policy decisions, balancing supply reliability, cost, and environmental impact, support sustainable long-term economic development
Energy source considerations and their environmental impacts have no relevance to national policy-making
Environmental impact should never be a factor considered in energy-related policy decisions
National energy policy is entirely disconnected from broader considerations of economic development
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Well- informed policy decisions, balancing supply reliability, cost, and environmental impact, support sustainable long-term economic development

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a machine’s actual mechanical output can never exceed its energy input, despite any mechanical advantage it might provide?
options: The principle of conservation of energy dictates that a machine cannot produce more output energy than the energy supplied to it; any apparent “advantage” comes from trading force for distance, not from creating additional energy
A well-designed machine can produce more output energy than the energy originally supplied to it
The principle of conservation of energy does not apply to mechanical systems involving simple machines
Mechanical advantage always corresponds directly to a net gain in total energy
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: The principle of conservation of energy dictates that a machine cannot produce more output energy than the energy supplied to it; any apparent “advantage” comes from trading force for distance, not from creating additional energy

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly explains why nuclear power, despite its significant energy output potential, requires stringent safety regulation and careful waste management?
options: Nuclear fission processes involve handling radioactive materials that can pose serious health and environmental risks if not properly controlled, necessitating strict safety and waste management protocols
Nuclear power generation poses no meaningful safety or environmental risk, requiring no particular regulation
Radioactive waste from nuclear power generation requires no special management considerations
Safety regulation is relevant only to fossil fuel power generation, not to nuclear power
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: Nuclear fission processes involve handling radioactive materials that can pose serious health and environmental risks if not properly controlled, necessitating strict safety and waste management protocols

Work, Energy and Power.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of the work-energy-power framework in mechanics and in broader considerations of energy and society?
options: This framework provides a unifying, quantitative basis for analysing mechanical processes and for evaluating and comparing different energy sources and their broader societal and environmental implications
Work, energy, and power concepts have no unifying relevance across mechanical analysis and broader energy considerations
These concepts apply only to purely theoretical mechanics, with no relevance to real- world energy policy or technology
Energy source comparison and evaluation can be conducted without any reference to fundamental work-energy-power concepts
Work, Energy and Power.correct_answer: This framework provides a unifying, quantitative basis for analysing mechanical processes and for evaluating and comparing different energy sources and their broader societal and environmental implications

Friction.text: Static friction is the frictional force that
options: acts on a body already in motion, opposing that motion
opposes the tendency of a stationary body to begin moving under an applied force
acts exclusively on moving fluids, never on solids
does not actually exist between any two surfaces
Friction.correct_answer: opposes the tendency of a stationary body to begin moving under an applied force

Friction.text: Kinetic (dynamic) friction is the frictional force that
options: opposes the relative sliding motion between two surfaces already in motion relative to each other
acts only on a body that remains completely stationary
is always greater in magnitude than limiting static friction, for the same surfaces
does not depend on the nature of the two surfaces in contact
Friction.correct_answer: opposes the relative sliding motion between two surfaces already in motion relative to each other

Friction.text: The coefficient of limiting friction between two surfaces is defined as the ratio of the
options: normal reaction to the limiting frictional force
limiting frictional force to the normal reaction between the two surfaces
applied force to the weight of the body
contact area to the applied normal force
Friction.correct_answer: limiting frictional force to the normal reaction between the two surfaces

Friction.text: A clear practical advantage of friction is that it
options: always wastes useful energy, with no compensating benefit
enables walking and allows vehicle tyres to grip the road surface effectively
invariably causes unwanted wear in all machine components
provides no benefit whatsoever in everyday life
Friction.correct_answer: enables walking and allows vehicle tyres to grip the road surface effectively

Friction.text: A key disadvantage of friction in machinery is that it
options: always improves overall machine efficiency
causes wear on moving parts and converts some useful mechanical energy into heat, reducing efficiency
has no negative consequences of any kind
always helps conserve energy within a machine
Friction.correct_answer: causes wear on moving parts and converts some useful mechanical energy into heat, reducing efficiency

Friction.text: Friction between moving machine parts can generally be reduced by
options: roughening the contacting surfaces further
applying a suitable lubricant, such as oil or grease, between the surfaces
increasing the normal force pressing the surfaces together
a method that has no bearing on the surfaces’ interaction
Friction.correct_answer: applying a suitable lubricant, such as oil or grease, between the surfaces

Friction.text: Viscosity refers to a fluid’s
options: colour
internal resistance to flow
density, considered in isolation from flow behaviour
temperature, considered in isolation from flow behaviour
Friction.correct_answer: internal resistance to flow

Friction.text: Terminal velocity of a body falling through a fluid is reached when
