options: the body continues to accelerate without limit
the net force on the body becomes zero, as the upward resistive (drag) force comes to balance the body’s weight
the body abruptly stops moving altogether
the body’s velocity becomes negative
Friction.correct_answer: the net force on the body becomes zero, as the upward resistive (drag) force comes to balance the body’s weight

Friction.text: According to Stoke’s law, the viscous drag force experienced by a small sphere moving through a fluid depends on the sphere’s radius, its velocity, and the fluid’s
options: colour
viscosity
temperature alone, with no reference to viscosity
mass, rather than its viscosity
Friction.correct_answer: viscosity

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly compares limiting static friction with kinetic friction, for the same pair of surfaces?
options: Limiting static friction is generally slightly greater than or equal to kinetic friction
Kinetic friction is always significantly greater than limiting static friction
They are always exactly equal in every case
There is no meaningful relationship between the two
Friction.correct_answer: Limiting static friction is generally slightly greater than or equal to kinetic friction

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why it is generally harder to get a heavy box moving from rest than to keep it moving once already sliding?
options: Static friction is typically greater than kinetic friction, so more force is required to overcome it initially
Static friction is typically less than kinetic friction
There is no meaningful difference between static and kinetic friction
Friction actually increases once an object begins moving
Friction.correct_answer: Static friction is typically greater than kinetic friction, so more force is required to overcome it initially

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why ball bearings are commonly used in rotating machine components to reduce friction?
options: They convert sliding friction into rolling friction, which is generally significantly lower for the same load
Ball bearings increase, rather than decrease, the friction present
Ball bearings have no measurable effect on friction
Ball bearings function by increasing surface contact area
Friction.correct_answer: They convert sliding friction into rolling friction, which is generally significantly lower for the same load

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a light object, such as a feather, reaches terminal velocity in air much sooner than a denser object of similar size?
options: The feather’s relatively large surface area compared to its weight allows air resistance to balance its weight much more quickly
Terminal velocity depends solely on an object’s colour
Denser objects always reach terminal velocity sooner than lighter objects of similar size
Air resistance is entirely unrelated to an object’s surface area or weight
Friction.correct_answer: The feather’s relatively large surface area compared to its weight allows air resistance to balance its weight much more quickly

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains a practical use of Stoke’s law, such as determining the viscosity of a liquid using a falling-sphere experiment?
options: Measuring the terminal velocity of a small sphere as it falls through the liquid, and applying Stoke’s law, allows the liquid’s viscosity to be calculated
Stoke’s law has no practical experimental application
Terminal velocity has no relationship to a fluid’s viscosity
Sphere size has no bearing on determining viscosity using Stoke’s law
Friction.correct_answer: Measuring the terminal velocity of a small sphere as it falls through the liquid, and applying Stoke’s law, allows the liquid’s viscosity to be calculated

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why streamlining the shape of a vehicle generally improves its fuel efficiency?
options: A streamlined shape reduces air resistance, lowering the energy required to overcome this resistance during motion
Streamlining has no effect on air resistance encountered by a moving vehicle
A streamlined shape always increases air resistance
Fuel efficiency is unrelated to a vehicle’s aerodynamic shape
Friction.correct_answer: A streamlined shape reduces air resistance, lowering the energy required to overcome this resistance during motion

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains the essential role of friction in the effective operation of a vehicle’s braking system?
options: Friction between the brake pads and the wheel (or disc) converts the vehicle’s kinetic energy into heat, thereby slowing it down
Friction plays no functional role in how vehicle brakes operate
Brakes function by completely eliminating friction at the relevant contact surfaces
Vehicle braking is entirely independent of any frictional forces
Friction.correct_answer: Friction between the brake pads and the wheel (or disc) converts the vehicle’s kinetic energy into heat, thereby slowing it down

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why walking on a wet, icy surface is generally more difficult than walking on a dry, rough surface?
options: Ice typically provides a much lower coefficient of friction than a dry, rough surface, reducing the grip available for walking
Ice generally provides more friction than a dry, rough surface
The coefficient of friction is essentially identical between ice and dry, rough surfaces
Friction has no relevance to the difficulty of walking on different surfaces
Friction.correct_answer: Ice typically provides a much lower coefficient of friction than a dry, rough surface, reducing the grip available for walking

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why increasing the roughness of two surfaces in contact generally increases the friction between them, up to a certain point?
options: Rougher surfaces typically have more microscopic interlocking irregularities, resisting relative sliding motion between them
Surface roughness has no bearing on the resulting frictional force
Rougher surfaces always reduce, rather than increase, the frictional force
Frictional force depends only on the mass of the interacting objects, not on surface roughness
Friction.correct_answer: Rougher surfaces typically have more microscopic interlocking irregularities, resisting relative sliding motion between them

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why raindrops falling through air generally reach a fairly constant (terminal) velocity, rather than continuing to accelerate indefinitely?
options: As a raindrop’s speed increases, air resistance increases correspondingly, until it balances the drop’s weight, resulting in zero net force and constant velocity
Raindrops continue accelerating indefinitely, with no limiting factor of any kind
Air resistance has no effect on the motion of a falling raindrop
Terminal velocity is entirely unrelated to the balance between weight and air resistance
Friction.correct_answer: As a raindrop’s speed increases, air resistance increases correspondingly, until it balances the drop’s weight, resulting in zero net force and constant velocity

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why applying oil to a squeaking door hinge typically eliminates the squeaking sound?
options: The oil reduces friction between the moving metal surfaces of the hinge, preventing the stick-slip motion that produces the squeaking sound
Applying oil has no effect on the friction present at the hinge
Oil always increases friction between hinge surfaces, worsening any squeaking
The squeaking sound has no relationship to friction between the hinge’s moving parts
Friction.correct_answer: The oil reduces friction between the moving metal surfaces of the hinge, preventing the stick-slip motion that produces the squeaking sound

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why engine oil viscosity is an important consideration for effective engine lubrication, particularly across a range of operating temperatures?
options: An oil that flows too sluggishly (high viscosity, especially when cold) or too freely (low viscosity, especially when hot) may fail to provide adequate lubrication under the relevant operating conditions
Oil viscosity has no bearing on how effectively an engine is lubricated
The ideal engine oil should have the highest possible viscosity, regardless of operating temperature
Engine lubrication is entirely unaffected by temperature-related viscosity changes
Friction.correct_answer: An oil that flows too sluggishly (high viscosity, especially when cold) or too freely (low viscosity, especially when hot) may fail to provide adequate lubrication under the relevant operating conditions

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a parachute significantly increases a falling person’s air resistance, allowing a much lower, safer terminal velocity to be reached?
options: The parachute greatly increases the effective surface area exposed to the air, substantially increasing the air resistance experienced for a given falling speed
A parachute has no effect on the air resistance experienced during a fall
A parachute reduces the surface area exposed to the air, decreasing air resistance
Terminal velocity is unrelated to the surface area of a falling object
Friction.correct_answer: The parachute greatly increases the effective surface area exposed to the air, substantially increasing the air resistance experienced for a given falling speed

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly explains why oil, rather than water, is generally preferred as a lubricant for metal machine parts?
options: Oil generally has superior adhesive and film-forming properties on metal surfaces, more effectively separating the moving surfaces and reducing direct metal-to-metal contact
Water is always a superior lubricant to oil for metal machine parts
The choice of lubricant has no bearing on the degree of friction reduction achieved
Oil and water are equally effective lubricants in every practical situation
Friction.correct_answer: Oil generally has superior adhesive and film-forming properties on metal surfaces, more effectively separating the moving surfaces and reducing direct metal-to-metal contact

Friction.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of understanding friction and viscosity in engineering design and everyday applications?
options: Understanding these concepts enables engineers and designers to balance the beneficial and detrimental effects of resistive forces, informing the design of efficient, safe machines, vehicles, and structures
Friction and viscosity concepts have no practical relevance to engineering design
Engineering and everyday applications require no consideration of frictional or viscous effects
Understanding these resistive forces is relevant only to abstract theoretical physics
Friction.correct_answer: Understanding these concepts enables engineers and designers to balance the beneficial and detrimental effects of resistive forces, informing the design of efficient, safe machines, vehicles, and structures

Simple Machines.text: A simple machine is a device that enables a force applied at one point to
options: always increase the total energy available within a system
overcome a resisting load at another point, generally making a task easier to perform
function only by reducing the effort required, with no other effect
operate without ever providing any mechanical advantage
Simple Machines.correct_answer: overcome a resisting load at another point, generally making a task easier to perform

Simple Machines.text: The mechanical advantage of a machine is the ratio of the
options: effort applied to the load overcome
load overcome to the effort applied
velocity ratio to the machine’s efficiency
work output to work input, expressed only when the two are equal
Simple Machines.correct_answer: load overcome to the effort applied

Simple Machines.text: The velocity ratio of a machine is the ratio of the
options: distance moved by the load to the distance moved by the effort, in the same time
distance moved by the effort to the distance moved by the load, in the same time
load overcome to the effort applied
work output to work input
Simple Machines.correct_answer: distance moved by the effort to the distance moved by the load, in the same time

Simple Machines.text: The efficiency of a machine is defined as the ratio of
options: mechanical advantage to velocity ratio, usually expressed as a percentage
load to effort alone
effort to load alone
input force to output force, without regard to distance moved
Simple Machines.correct_answer: mechanical advantage to velocity ratio, usually expressed as a percentage

Simple Machines.text: For a perfectly (ideally) efficient machine, mechanical advantage would be
options: always greater than the velocity ratio
exactly equal to the velocity ratio, corresponding to 100% efficiency
always exactly zero
entirely unrelated to the velocity ratio
Simple Machines.correct_answer: exactly equal to the velocity ratio, corresponding to 100% efficiency

Simple Machines.text: Real machines in practice generally have an efficiency that is
options: always exactly 100%, with no losses of any kind
less than 100%, primarily due to energy losses such as friction
always greater than 100%
entirely unrelated to any frictional losses
Simple Machines.correct_answer: less than 100%, primarily due to energy losses such as friction

Simple Machines.text: A lever is a simple machine that operates according to the principle of
options: fluid pressure transmission
moments (the turning effect of forces) about a fixed pivot, called the fulcrum
electromagnetic induction
the refraction of light
Simple Machines.correct_answer: moments (the turning effect of forces) about a fixed pivot, called the fulcrum

Simple Machines.text: In a first-class lever, the fulcrum is positioned
options: between the effort and the load
at the same end as the effort
at the same end as the load
at no defined position relative to the effort and load
Simple Machines.correct_answer: between the effort and the load

Simple Machines.text: A pulley system is primarily used to
options: change the direction and/or magnitude of an applied force to make lifting a load easier
generate electrical energy directly
measure temperature accurately
measure short time intervals
Simple Machines.correct_answer: change the direction and/or magnitude of an applied force to make lifting a load easier

Simple Machines.text: An inclined plane provides a mechanical advantage by allowing a load to be raised using
options: a smaller effort exerted over a proportionally longer distance, compared to lifting it vertically
a larger effort exerted over a shorter distance
no effort whatsoever
an effort and distance identical to those required for direct vertical lifting
Simple Machines.correct_answer: a smaller effort exerted over a proportionally longer distance, compared to lifting it vertically

Simple Machines.text: A screw can be regarded as a simple machine based fundamentally on the principle of
options: the lever
an inclined plane wound around a central cylinder
fluid pressure transmission
electromagnetic induction
Simple Machines.correct_answer: an inclined plane wound around a central cylinder

Simple Machines.text: If a machine has a mechanical advantage of 3 and a velocity ratio of 4, its efficiency is
Which of the following correctly explains why the efficiency of any real, practical machine is always less than 100%?
options: Some portion of the input energy is inevitably lost, typically to friction and similar resistive effects, rather than being entirely converted into useful output work
Real machines always convert 100% of input energy into useful output work
Efficiency losses occur only in electrically powered machines, never in purely mechanical ones
There is no relationship between friction and a machine’s overall efficiency
Simple Machines.correct_answer: Some portion of the input energy is inevitably lost, typically to friction and similar resistive effects, rather than being entirely converted into useful output work

Simple Machines.text: A single, fixed pulley chiefly provides which of the following benefits?
options: A significant mechanical advantage substantially greater than 1
A change in the direction of the applied effort, generally with a mechanical advantage close to 1
No practical benefit whatsoever
An automatic increase in the load’s actual weight
Simple Machines.correct_answer: A change in the direction of the applied effort, generally with a mechanical advantage close to 1

Simple Machines.text: A block-and-tackle pulley system achieves mechanical advantage mainly by
options: using multiple pulleys and rope segments to share the supported load across several strands of rope
relying on a single rope with no additional supporting pulleys
directly increasing the load’s actual weight
a mechanism unrelated to the number of pulleys used
Simple Machines.correct_answer: using multiple pulleys and rope segments to share the supported load across several strands of rope

Simple Machines.text: Which of the following correctly explains why gears are considered a form of simple machine?
options: They transmit and can modify rotational force and speed between connected shafts, operating on principles similar to a wheel and axle
Gears have no meaningful relationship to simple machine principles
Gears can only ever reduce mechanical advantage, never increase it
Gears function purely through optical, rather than mechanical, principles
Simple Machines.correct_answer: They transmit and can modify rotational force and speed between connected shafts, operating on principles similar to a wheel and axle

Simple Machines.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a longer ramp, for a given total height, generally requires a smaller effort force to move a load up it, compared to a shorter, steeper ramp of the same height?
options: A longer ramp has a smaller angle of inclination, distributing the same total work over a greater distance, thereby requiring a proportionally smaller effort force
Ramp length has no bearing on the effort force required
A longer ramp always requires a greater, rather than smaller, effort force
Effort force required is entirely unrelated to a ramp’s length or angle of inclination
Simple Machines.correct_answer: A longer ramp has a smaller angle of inclination, distributing the same total work over a greater distance, thereby requiring a proportionally smaller effort force

Simple Machines.text: Which of the following correctly explains why simple machines, while reducing the effort force needed, do not reduce the total work required to raise a given load through a given height (ignoring friction)?
options: By the principle of conservation of energy, any reduction in effort force is offset by a corresponding increase in the distance over which that effort must act, keeping the total work roughly constant for an ideal, frictionless machine
Simple machines always reduce the total work required, in apparent violation of energy conservation
Work done has no relationship whatsoever to either force or distance moved
There is no meaningful trade-off between effort force and distance moved in a simple machine
Simple Machines.correct_answer: By the principle of conservation of energy, any reduction in effort force is offset by a corresponding increase in the distance over which that effort must act, keeping the total work roughly constant for an ideal, frictionless machine

Simple Machines.text: Which of the following correctly explains a practical, everyday application of the lever principle?
options: Using a crowbar to lift a heavy object, applying a relatively small effort over a large distance from the fulcrum, compared to the load’s distance
Levers have no meaningful everyday, practical applications
Levers can only be applied within highly specialized industrial equipment
The action of a crowbar is unrelated to the lever principle
Simple Machines.correct_answer: Using a crowbar to lift a heavy object, applying a relatively small effort over a large distance from the fulcrum, compared to the load’s distance

Simple Machines.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a hydraulic jack, considered as a simple machine, can provide substantial mechanical advantage?
options: A relatively small force applied over a small piston area can, through Pascal’s principle of pressure transmission, produce a much larger force over a larger piston area
Hydraulic jacks have no meaningful relationship to simple machine principles
Hydraulic jacks always require an effort force greater than the load being lifted
Pascal’s principle plays no role in the mechanical advantage a hydraulic jack provides
Simple Machines.correct_answer: A relatively small force applied over a small piston area can, through Pascal’s principle of pressure transmission, produce a much larger force over a larger piston area

Simple Machines.text: Which of the following correctly explains why regularly lubricating the moving parts of a machine generally improves its overall efficiency?
options: Lubrication reduces frictional losses, allowing a greater proportion of the input energy to be usefully converted into output work
Lubrication has no measurable effect on a machine’s overall efficiency
Lubrication generally decreases, rather than increases, machine efficiency
Friction has no bearing on a machine’s overall efficiency
Simple Machines.correct_answer: Lubrication reduces frictional losses, allowing a greater proportion of the input energy to be usefully converted into output work

Simple Machines.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding both mechanical advantage and velocity ratio is important when selecting an appropriate machine for a specific practical task?
options: It allows an appropriate trade-off to be made between the effort force required and the resulting distance or speed of operation, matching the machine to the task’s specific requirements
Mechanical advantage and velocity ratio are irrelevant when selecting a suitable machine for a task
All simple machines provide identical mechanical advantage, regardless of their design
Velocity ratio has no bearing on how a machine should be chosen for a particular application
Simple Machines.correct_answer: It allows an appropriate trade-off to be made between the effort force required and the resulting distance or speed of operation, matching the machine to the task’s specific requirements

Simple Machines.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a wheelbarrow is classified as a second-class lever, with the load positioned between the fulcrum (wheel) and the effort?
options: In a second-class lever, the load lies between the fulcrum and the effort, which matches the typical arrangement of a wheelbarrow, where the wheel acts as the fulcrum, the load sits in the middle, and the effort is applied at the handles
A wheelbarrow is more correctly classified as a first-class lever, with the fulcrum between the load and effort
Lever classification has no relevance to the design or operation of a wheelbarrow
A wheelbarrow does not operate according to any lever principle
Simple Machines.correct_answer: In a second-class lever, the load lies between the fulcrum and the effort, which matches the typical arrangement of a wheelbarrow, where the wheel acts as the fulcrum, the load sits in the middle, and the effort is applied at the handles

Simple Machines.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of simple machines in mechanics and everyday engineering applications?
options: Simple machines enable tasks requiring large forces or precise motion control to be accomplished more practically, forming the conceptual basis for countless mechanical devices and systems
Simple machines have no significant role in mechanics or everyday engineering applications
Simple machine principles are relevant only to purely abstract, theoretical physics problems
Modern engineering has entirely superseded the relevance of simple machine principles
Simple Machines.correct_answer: Simple machines enable tasks requiring large forces or precise motion control to be accomplished more practically, forming the conceptual basis for countless mechanical devices and systems

Elasticity.text: Elasticity is a material’s ability to
options: undergo permanent deformation under any applied force
return to its original shape and size once a deforming force has been removed
break immediately upon the application of any force
remain entirely undeformed under any circumstances
Elasticity.correct_answer: return to its original shape and size once a deforming force has been removed

Elasticity.text: The elastic limit of a material marks the point beyond which
options: the material still returns fully to its original shape once the force is removed
the material no longer returns completely to its original shape when the force is removed, and permanent deformation begins
the material becomes completely incapable of any deformation
Hooke’s law continues to apply indefinitely, with no limit
Elasticity.correct_answer: the material no longer returns completely to its original shape when the force is removed, and permanent deformation begins

Elasticity.text: Hooke’s law states that, within the elastic limit, a material’s extension is
options: inversely proportional to the applied force
directly proportional to the applied force
entirely independent of the applied force
always exactly zero, regardless of applied force
Elasticity.correct_answer: directly proportional to the applied force

Elasticity.text: Young’s modulus of a material is defined as the ratio of
options: extension to original length alone
stress to strain, within the material’s elastic limit
force to extension alone, without reference to the sample’s dimensions
mass to volume
Elasticity.correct_answer: stress to strain, within the material’s elastic limit

Elasticity.text: A spring balance measures force (or weight) based on the principle that, within its elastic limit, a spring’s
options: mass changes proportionally with applied force
extension is proportional to the applied force, according to Hooke’s law
colour changes measurably with applied force
temperature changes proportionally with applied force
Elasticity.correct_answer: extension is proportional to the applied force, according to Hooke’s law

Elasticity.text: The work done in stretching a spring within its elastic limit, by extension x with spring constant k, is calculated as
options: kx
½kx²
kx²
k/x
Elasticity.correct_answer: ½kx²

Elasticity.text: Stress, as used in the study of elasticity, is defined as
options: force per unit cross-sectional area
extension per unit original length
force multiplied by extension
mass per unit volume
Elasticity.correct_answer: force per unit cross-sectional area

Elasticity.text: Strain, as used in the study of elasticity, is defined as
options: force per unit area
extension (or change in length) per unit original length
force multiplied by original length
mass per unit length
Elasticity.correct_answer: extension (or change in length) per unit original length

Elasticity.text: A material obeying Hooke’s law shows a force-extension graph that is
options: a curve throughout its entire range
a straight line passing through the origin, up to the elastic limit
always perfectly horizontal
always perfectly vertical
Elasticity.correct_answer: a straight line passing through the origin, up to the elastic limit

Elasticity.text: Which of the following materials would typically be described as ductile, capable of being significantly stretched before eventually breaking?
options: Glass
Copper wire
A typical ceramic
Cast iron, in general
Elasticity.correct_answer: Copper wire

Elasticity.text: Which of the following materials would typically be described as brittle, tending to break with relatively little prior deformation?
options: Rubber
Copper
Glass
A typical steel wire
Elasticity.correct_answer: Glass

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why stretching a spring beyond its elastic limit results in a permanent change to its shape?
options: Beyond the elastic limit, the material’s internal structure is permanently altered, so it no longer fully returns to its original shape once the deforming force is removed
The elastic limit has no bearing on whether permanent deformation occurs
Materials always fully return to their original shape, regardless of how far they are stretched
Permanent deformation can only ever occur below the elastic limit, never beyond it
Elasticity.correct_answer: Beyond the elastic limit, the material’s internal structure is permanently altered, so it no longer fully returns to its original shape once the deforming force is removed

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why Young’s modulus is generally regarded as a property intrinsic to a particular material, rather than a property of a specific object made from that material?
options: Because Young’s modulus is derived from stress and strain, which already account for cross-sectional area and original length, its value is independent of the specific dimensions of a given sample
Young’s modulus varies significantly with the particular size or shape of any given object
Young’s modulus depends only on the mass of an object, rather than on the inherent properties of the material
There is no meaningful distinction between a material’s Young’s modulus and a specific object’s overall stiffness
Elasticity.correct_answer: Because Young’s modulus is derived from stress and strain, which already account for cross-sectional area and original length, its value is independent of the specific dimensions of a given sample

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a spring balance provides a reliable measurement of force, provided it is used within the spring’s elastic limit?
options: Within the elastic limit, extension is directly proportional to the applied force (Hooke’s law), so a calibrated scale can reliably relate a given extension to a corresponding force
A spring balance functions equally reliably whether used within or beyond its elastic limit
There is no meaningful relationship between a spring’s extension and the force applied to it
A spring balance actually measures mass directly, with no relevance to force or extension
Elasticity.correct_answer: Within the elastic limit, extension is directly proportional to the applied force (Hooke’s law), so a calibrated scale can reliably relate a given extension to a corresponding force

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why steel cables selected for suspension bridges must be carefully chosen based on their elastic properties and breaking strength?
options: The cables must reliably support significant loads while remaining within their elastic limit under normal conditions, and must have a breaking strength providing an appropriate margin of safety above the maximum expected load
Elastic properties and breaking strength have no relevance to selecting appropriate suspension bridge cables
Suspension bridge cables are typically selected without any regard to expected loads
Breaking strength has no bearing on structural safety considerations for such cables
Elasticity.correct_answer: The cables must reliably support significant loads while remaining within their elastic limit under normal conditions, and must have a breaking strength providing an appropriate margin of safety above the maximum expected load

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a rubber band often shows a noticeably non-linear force-extension relationship, deviating from simple Hooke’s law behaviour, even at relatively modest extensions?
options: Rubber’s molecular structure, consisting of long, coiled polymer chains, behaves quite differently under applied stress compared to the more regular, crystalline lattice structure typical of most metals
Rubber always follows Hooke’s law precisely, identically to a typical metal spring
There is no meaningful structural difference between rubber and typical metals relevant to their elastic behaviour
Metals never obey Hooke’s law, unlike rubber, which always does
Elasticity.correct_answer: Rubber’s molecular structure, consisting of long, coiled polymer chains, behaves quite differently under applied stress compared to the more regular, crystalline lattice structure typical of most metals

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains the practical significance of elastic energy storage, such as in a stretched catapult or bowstring?
options: The elastic potential energy stored while stretching is subsequently converted into kinetic energy upon release, propelling a projectile forward
Elastic energy storage has no practical relevance to devices such as catapults or bows
Such devices function through purely magnetic principles, unrelated to elasticity
Stretching a catapult or bowstring involves no meaningful storage of elastic potential energy
Elasticity.correct_answer: The elastic potential energy stored while stretching is subsequently converted into kinetic energy upon release, propelling a projectile forward

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why engineers must know a material’s elastic limit and Young’s modulus before using it in load-bearing structural components, such as building beams?
options: This information allows accurate prediction of how much a component will deform under expected loads, ensuring it remains safely within its elastic (recoverable) range during normal service
Elastic limit and Young’s modulus have no relevance to structural engineering decisions
Structural components are generally designed without any reference to a material’s elastic properties
Beams deform identically regardless of the specific material’s elastic characteristics
Elasticity.correct_answer: This information allows accurate prediction of how much a component will deform under expected loads, ensuring it remains safely within its elastic (recoverable) range during normal service

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why two springs made of identical material, but with different coil geometry, such as differing wire thickness or coil diameter, can have different spring constants?
options: A spring’s constant depends not only on the inherent elastic properties of the material but also on the specific geometric details of the spring’s construction, such as wire thickness and coil diameter
Spring constant depends solely on the material, regardless of any geometric factors
All springs constructed from an identical material necessarily have identical spring constants
Spring geometry has no bearing whatsoever on a spring’s mechanical behaviour
Elasticity.correct_answer: A spring’s constant depends not only on the inherent elastic properties of the material but also on the specific geometric details of the spring’s construction, such as wire thickness and coil diameter

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why repeatedly stretching a material beyond its elastic limit, even without immediate breakage, can progressively weaken it over time (a phenomenon related to material fatigue)?
options: Repeated permanent (plastic) deformation can introduce accumulating microscopic structural damage, progressively reducing the material’s overall strength and increasing the likelihood of eventual failure
Repeated stretching beyond the elastic limit has no cumulative effect on a material’s strength
Materials generally become progressively stronger when repeatedly stretched beyond their elastic limit
Fatigue has no meaningful relationship to a material’s elastic limit
Elasticity.correct_answer: Repeated permanent (plastic) deformation can introduce accumulating microscopic structural damage, progressively reducing the material’s overall strength and increasing the likelihood of eventual failure

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why an elastic string or rubber band used to launch a small projectile stores more energy when stretched further, up to a limit?
options: Elastic potential energy stored generally increases with the square of the extension (for material obeying Hooke’s law), so greater extension results in significantly more stored energy, up to the elastic limit
Elastic potential energy stored has no relationship to the extent to which the material is stretched
Greater extension always results in less stored elastic potential energy
Elastic potential energy storage is unrelated to the concept of extension at all
Elasticity.correct_answer: Elastic potential energy stored generally increases with the square of the extension (for material obeying Hooke’s law), so greater extension results in significantly more stored energy, up to the elastic limit

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the same total extension of a spring, achieved via a smaller force applied gradually versus a larger, sudden force, can nonetheless correspond to differing amounts of work actually done, especially if the elastic limit is exceeded in one case?
options: If a sudden, larger force exceeds the material’s elastic limit, some of the resulting deformation becomes permanent, and the work-extension relationship departs from the simple, reversible elastic (Hooke’s law) case applicable at smaller, gradually applied forces
The manner in which a force is applied (gradually or suddenly) never has any bearing on the resulting work done or deformation behaviour
Exceeding the elastic limit has no relevance to how work done relates to the resulting extension
Work done in deforming a spring is always identical regardless of whether the elastic limit is exceeded
Elasticity.correct_answer: If a sudden, larger force exceeds the material’s elastic limit, some of the resulting deformation becomes permanent, and the work-extension relationship departs from the simple, reversible elastic (Hooke’s law) case applicable at smaller, gradually applied forces

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly explains why bungee cords are specifically designed to be highly elastic, capable of substantial, safe extension?
options: A highly elastic cord can absorb and gradually dissipate the significant kinetic energy of a falling person over a large extension distance, resulting in a much lower peak force (and safer deceleration) than a less elastic material would provide
Bungee cords are designed to be as inelastic (rigid) as possible, for maximum safety
Elasticity has no relevance to the safety or functional design of a bungee cord
A less elastic cord would provide equally safe deceleration for a falling person
Elasticity.correct_answer: A highly elastic cord can absorb and gradually dissipate the significant kinetic energy of a falling person over a large extension distance, resulting in a much lower peak force (and safer deceleration) than a less elastic material would provide

Elasticity.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of studying elasticity, Hooke’s law, and Young’s modulus within physics and engineering?
options: These concepts underpin the design and safety analysis of countless structures and devices, from simple springs to major engineering structures, helping ensure materials perform reliably under their expected loads
Elasticity concepts have no meaningful application within engineering or structural design
Hooke’s law and Young’s modulus are relevant only to abstract, purely theoretical physics, with no practical use
Structural safety analysis can be reliably conducted without any consideration of a material’s elastic properties
Elasticity.correct_answer: These concepts underpin the design and safety analysis of countless structures and devices, from simple springs to major engineering structures, helping ensure materials perform reliably under their expected loads

Pressure.text: Atmospheric pressure is defined as the pressure exerted at a given point by the
options: weight of a liquid column above that point
weight of the column of air in the atmosphere above that point
enclosed gas within a sealed container only
sun’s radiant energy alone
Pressure.correct_answer: weight of the column of air in the atmosphere above that point

Pressure.text: The SI unit of pressure is the
options: newton
pascal
joule
watt
Pressure.correct_answer: pascal

Pressure.text: A simple mercury barometer is designed to measure
options: temperature
atmospheric pressure
humidity directly
the speed of sound in air
Pressure.correct_answer: atmospheric pressure

Pressure.text: An aneroid barometer measures atmospheric pressure using
options: a column of mercury
the mechanical response of a partially evacuated, flexible metal chamber
a column of water
an electrical resistance thermometer
Pressure.correct_answer: the mechanical response of a partially evacuated, flexible metal chamber

Pressure.text: A manometer is generally used to measure
options: temperature
the pressure difference between a gas supply and the surrounding atmosphere, typically using a liquid column
humidity
short time intervals
Pressure.correct_answer: the pressure difference between a gas supply and the surrounding atmosphere, typically using a liquid column

Pressure.text: As altitude above sea level increases, atmospheric pressure generally
options: increases
decreases, since there is progressively less air above any given point
remains completely unchanged
becomes negative
Pressure.correct_answer: decreases, since there is progressively less air above any given point

Pressure.text: The pressure at depth h within a liquid of density ρ is given by
options: P = ρg/h
P = ρgh
P = ρ/(gh)
P = gh/ρ
Pressure.correct_answer: P = ρgh

Pressure.text: According to this relationship, pressure within a liquid increases with
options: decreasing depth
increasing depth (and increasing density), at a given location
decreasing density only, with no dependence on depth
neither depth nor density
Pressure.correct_answer: increasing depth (and increasing density), at a given location

Pressure.text: Pascal’s principle states that pressure applied to an enclosed, incompressible fluid is
options: absorbed entirely at the point of application, with no transmission elsewhere
transmitted equally in all directions throughout the fluid
transmitted only in the downward direction
substantially reduced as it travels through the fluid
Pressure.correct_answer: transmitted equally in all directions throughout the fluid

Pressure.text: A hydraulic press (or hydraulic jack) functions according to
options: Boyle’s law
Pascal’s principle of pressure transmission through an enclosed fluid
Archimedes’ principle
Newton’s third law of motion alone, with no reference to fluid pressure
Pressure.correct_answer: Pascal’s principle of pressure transmission through an enclosed fluid

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a hydraulic jack can lift a heavy vehicle using a comparatively small applied force?
options: A small force applied over a small piston area generates a pressure that, transmitted equally throughout the fluid, produces a much larger force acting over a larger piston area
Hydraulic jacks function purely through a mechanical lever arrangement, with no relationship to fluid pressure
The applied force is always exactly equal to the lifted load’s weight, providing no mechanical advantage
Fluid pressure has no functional role in how a hydraulic jack operates
Pressure.correct_answer: A small force applied over a small piston area generates a pressure that, transmitted equally throughout the fluid, produces a much larger force acting over a larger piston area

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why deep-sea divers experience significantly greater pressure than swimmers near the water’s surface?
options: Pressure within a liquid increases with depth, due to the increasing weight of the liquid column situated above a given point
Pressure within a liquid is entirely independent of depth
Pressure within a liquid decreases as depth increases
Only the liquid’s density, and never its depth, determines the pressure at a given point
Pressure.correct_answer: Pressure within a liquid increases with depth, due to the increasing weight of the liquid column situated above a given point

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains the operating principle of a simple mercury barometer used to measure atmospheric pressure?
options: Atmospheric pressure supports a column of mercury inside an inverted, sealed tube, with the resulting height of the mercury column being directly related to the prevailing atmospheric pressure
A mercury barometer measures pressure by directly weighing the mercury on a scale
The height of mercury in a barometer bears no relationship to atmospheric pressure
A mercury barometer can only measure liquid pressure, never atmospheric pressure
Pressure.correct_answer: Atmospheric pressure supports a column of mercury inside an inverted, sealed tube, with the resulting height of the mercury column being directly related to the prevailing atmospheric pressure

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why aircraft cabins require artificial pressurization during high-altitude flight?
options: Atmospheric pressure at high altitude is far too low to support normal human respiration and comfort, so cabin pressurization maintains conditions closer to those experienced at lower, more comfortable altitudes
Cabin pressurization has no relationship to the actual atmospheric pressure at cruising altitude
Atmospheric pressure increases considerably with altitude, requiring pressure reduction inside the cabin instead
Cabin pressurization exists solely for temperature control, with no relevance to pressure itself
Pressure.correct_answer: Atmospheric pressure at high altitude is far too low to support normal human respiration and comfort, so cabin pressurization maintains conditions closer to those experienced at lower, more comfortable altitudes

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why sucking through a drinking straw allows liquid to rise into the mouth?
options: Sucking reduces the air pressure inside the straw below atmospheric pressure, allowing the greater atmospheric pressure acting on the liquid’s surface to push the liquid up into the straw
Liquid rises in a straw purely due to gravity, with no relevance to any pressure difference
Atmospheric pressure plays no functional role in how a drinking straw works
Straws function by creating a total vacuum that directly pulls liquid upward, with no involvement of atmospheric pressure
Pressure.correct_answer: Sucking reduces the air pressure inside the straw below atmospheric pressure, allowing the greater atmospheric pressure acting on the liquid’s surface to push the liquid up into the straw

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the specific choice of barometric liquid, such as mercury rather than water, significantly affects the practical height of a barometer’s liquid column?
options: A denser liquid, such as mercury, requires a considerably shorter column to balance a given atmospheric pressure than a less dense liquid, such as water, would require
The density of the liquid used in a barometer has no bearing on the required column height
Water would require a shorter column than mercury to balance an identical atmospheric pressure
All liquids require an identical column height, regardless of their density, to balance a given atmospheric pressure
Pressure.correct_answer: A denser liquid, such as mercury, requires a considerably shorter column to balance a given atmospheric pressure than a less dense liquid, such as water, would require

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why submarine hulls must be structurally reinforced to withstand significant external water pressure at depth?
options: Water pressure increases substantially with depth, exerting considerable inward force on a submarine’s hull, requiring robust structural design to prevent collapse
Water pressure decreases with depth, so submarines actually require little structural reinforcement
Pressure at depth has no bearing on how a submarine’s hull should be structurally designed
A submarine’s hull experiences no meaningful external pressure, regardless of operating depth
Pressure.correct_answer: Water pressure increases substantially with depth, exerting considerable inward force on a submarine’s hull, requiring robust structural design to prevent collapse

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why hydraulic braking systems in vehicles rely fundamentally on the near-incompressibility of the brake fluid used?
options: Because the fluid is essentially incompressible, pressure applied at the brake pedal is transmitted almost instantaneously and effectively throughout the hydraulic system to the brake pads
Hydraulic brake fluid is highly compressible, which is actually essential for effective braking
The incompressibility of brake fluid has no functional relevance to how hydraulic brakes operate
Hydraulic brakes function purely through mechanical linkages, with no involvement of fluid pressure transmission
Pressure.correct_answer: Because the fluid is essentially incompressible, pressure applied at the brake pedal is transmitted almost instantaneously and effectively throughout the hydraulic system to the brake pads

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why elevated water storage towers are typically built at significant height above the areas they are intended to supply?
options: The resulting height difference creates sufficient water pressure, based on the depth-pressure relationship, to deliver an adequate water supply through pipes to consumers, without requiring continuous pumping
A water tower’s height has no bearing on the pressure ultimately delivered to consumers
Water towers are typically built at height purely for aesthetic reasons, unrelated to pressure considerations
Pressure delivered to consumers is completely independent of a water tower’s height
Pressure.correct_answer: The resulting height difference creates sufficient water pressure, based on the depth-pressure relationship, to deliver an adequate water supply through pipes to consumers, without requiring continuous pumping

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the pressure at the bottom of two containers holding the same liquid at the same depth, but having very different base areas, would nonetheless be identical, despite potentially very different total forces acting on their bases?
options: Liquid pressure depends only on depth and density (and gravitational field strength), not on the total base area of the container, even though the total force (pressure multiplied by area) may differ considerably
Liquid pressure primarily depends on a container’s base area, rather than on the depth of liquid
Containers with differing base areas will always show different pressures at an identical depth, regardless of the liquid or depth involved
Pressure and force are essentially identical concepts, with no meaningful distinction between them
Pressure.correct_answer: Liquid pressure depends only on depth and density (and gravitational field strength), not on the total base area of the container, even though the total force (pressure multiplied by area) may differ considerably

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why atmospheric pressure readings, such as those from a barometer, can be used to assist in weather forecasting?
options: Changes in atmospheric pressure are often associated with approaching changes in weather conditions, such as the arrival of a low-pressure system typically associated with unsettled weather
Atmospheric pressure bears no meaningful relationship to weather conditions
Barometric readings are useful only for determining altitude, never for weather-related purposes
Weather forecasting relies entirely on temperature measurements, with no relevance to atmospheric pressure
Pressure.correct_answer: Changes in atmospheric pressure are often associated with approaching changes in weather conditions, such as the arrival of a low-pressure system typically associated with unsettled weather

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a bicycle or car tyre must be inflated to a specific recommended pressure, rather than simply “as much as possible”?
options: Correct tyre pressure balances performance factors such as grip, fuel efficiency, and ride comfort, against risks such as excessive tyre wear or reduced structural safety margin if significantly overinflated
Tyre pressure has no bearing on vehicle performance, safety, or efficiency
Tyres should always be inflated to the maximum physically possible pressure for optimal performance
There is no recommended or appropriate pressure range for vehicle tyres
Pressure.correct_answer: Correct tyre pressure balances performance factors such as grip, fuel efficiency, and ride comfort, against risks such as excessive tyre wear or reduced structural safety margin if significantly overinflated

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the human ear can sometimes “pop” during rapid changes in altitude, such as during a flight’s ascent or descent?
options: Changes in external atmospheric pressure can create a temporary pressure imbalance between the middle ear and the outside environment, which is resolved (with a “popping” sensation) as air pressure equalizes via the Eustachian tube
Ear “popping” has no relationship whatsoever to changes in atmospheric pressure
Atmospheric pressure remains completely constant during changes in altitude, such as during a flight
The middle ear is entirely unaffected by any external atmospheric pressure changes
Pressure.correct_answer: Changes in external atmospheric pressure can create a temporary pressure imbalance between the middle ear and the outside environment, which is resolved (with a “popping” sensation) as air pressure equalizes via the Eustachian tube

Pressure.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of understanding pressure concepts, including atmospheric pressure, liquid pressure, and Pascal’s principle, in engineering and everyday technology?
options: These concepts underpin technologies ranging from hydraulic systems and aircraft cabin design to water supply systems and weather forecasting instruments
Pressure concepts have no meaningful practical relevance to engineering or everyday technology
Only theoretical physics benefits from understanding pressure, with no genuine real-world engineering application
Atmospheric and liquid pressure concepts bear no relation to practical technology of any kind
Pressure.correct_answer: These concepts underpin technologies ranging from hydraulic systems and aircraft cabin design to water supply systems and weather forecasting instruments

Liquids at Rest.text: Density of a substance is defined as its
options: mass per unit volume
volume per unit mass
weight per unit area
mass multiplied by its volume
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: mass per unit volume

Liquids at Rest.text: Relative density (specific gravity) of a substance is the ratio of
options: its density to the density of water, usually at a specified reference temperature
its mass to its volume directly, with no reference substance involved
its weight to its mass
its volume to the volume of an equal mass of water
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: its density to the density of water, usually at a specified reference temperature

Liquids at Rest.text: Upthrust on a body immersed in a fluid refers to the
options: downward force exerted by the fluid on the body
upward force exerted by the fluid on the body, opposing its weight
force experienced only by floating bodies, never by fully submerged ones
force always exactly equal to the body’s actual weight, regardless of the fluid
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: upward force exerted by the fluid on the body, opposing its weight

Liquids at Rest.text: Archimedes’ principle states that the upthrust experienced by a body wholly or partly immersed in a fluid is equal to the
options: weight of the body itself
weight of fluid displaced by the immersed portion of the body
volume of the body alone
density of the fluid alone
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: weight of fluid displaced by the immersed portion of the body

Liquids at Rest.text: The law of floatation states that a floating body displaces a weight of fluid equal to
options: its own volume
its own weight
the density of the fluid
exactly twice its own weight
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: its own weight

Liquids at Rest.text: A body floats in a given liquid when its average density is
options: greater than the density of the liquid
less than or equal to the density of the liquid
always exactly equal to the density of air
entirely unrelated to the density of the liquid
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: less than or equal to the density of the liquid

Liquids at Rest.text: A hydrometer is an instrument specifically designed to measure the
options: temperature of a liquid
relative density (specific gravity) of a liquid
viscosity of a liquid alone
volume of a liquid directly
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: relative density (specific gravity) of a liquid

Liquids at Rest.text: A hydrometer floats higher when placed in a liquid of
options: lower density
higher density
any density, floating at an identical level regardless
it always sinks fully, irrespective of density
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: higher density

Liquids at Rest.text: A steel ship, despite being constructed largely from dense steel, is able to float mainly because
options: steel itself has a density lower than that of water
the overall (average) density of the ship’s hull, including its enclosed air spaces, is less than the density of water
ships generally sink, contrary to everyday observation
floatation bears no relationship to an object’s average density
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: the overall (average) density of the ship’s hull, including its enclosed air spaces, is less than the density of water

Liquids at Rest.text: The density of a regularly shaped solid can be found experimentally by
options: measuring its mass and calculating its volume from its known dimensions
measuring only its mass, without any reference to volume
measuring only its dimensions, without any reference to mass
a method that cannot be applied experimentally
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: measuring its mass and calculating its volume from its known dimensions

Liquids at Rest.text: The density of an irregularly shaped solid can be found experimentally by
options: measuring its mass, and determining its volume by liquid displacement
measuring only its length
a method that cannot be applied to irregular solids
using a thermometer exclusively
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: measuring its mass, and determining its volume by liquid displacement

Liquids at Rest.text: According to Archimedes’ principle, a body of volume V, when completely submerged in a liquid of density ρ, experiences an upthrust of
options: V/ρ
Vρg
V + ρ
ρg/V
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: Vρg

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a solid lump of iron sinks in water, while a hollow iron ship floats?
options: The hollow ship’s overall shape displaces a much larger volume of water for the same total mass, reducing its average density below that of water, unlike the solid iron lump
A solid iron lump and a hollow iron ship necessarily have identical average densities
Iron always floats in water, regardless of its shape
An object’s shape has no bearing on whether it floats or sinks
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: The hollow ship’s overall shape displaces a much larger volume of water for the same total mass, reducing its average density below that of water, unlike the solid iron lump

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a hydrometer used for a specific application, such as testing battery acid, is typically calibrated with a specific scale?
options: The depth to which the hydrometer floats corresponds directly to the density of the surrounding liquid, allowing a calibrated scale to give a direct density (or concentration) reading
A hydrometer provides no useful information regarding a liquid’s density
A hydrometer’s floating depth bears no relationship to the surrounding liquid’s density
Hydrometers can only be used with pure water, and no other liquid
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: The depth to which the hydrometer floats corresponds directly to the density of the surrounding liquid, allowing a calibrated scale to give a direct density (or concentration) reading

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a swimmer floats more easily in the sea than in an ordinary freshwater swimming pool?
options: Seawater generally has a somewhat higher density than fresh water, due to its dissolved salt content, providing greater upthrust for a given submerged body volume
Seawater has a lower density than fresh water, making floating more difficult
Salinity has no meaningful effect on a liquid’s density or the upthrust it provides
People float with equal ease in any body of water, regardless of salinity
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: Seawater generally has a somewhat higher density than fresh water, due to its dissolved salt content, providing greater upthrust for a given submerged body volume

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains the practical use of Archimedes’ principle in controlling the buoyancy of a submarine?
options: A submarine adjusts its average density, by controlling the amount of water or air held in its ballast tanks, thereby controlling whether it floats, sinks, or remains at a constant depth
A submarine has no practical means of controlling its own buoyancy
Archimedes’ principle bears no relevance to submarine design or operation
Submarines always sink, regardless of how their ballast tanks are configured
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: A submarine adjusts its average density, by controlling the amount of water or air held in its ballast tanks, thereby controlling whether it floats, sinks, or remains at a constant depth

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains why measuring relative density, rather than absolute density alone, is often practically convenient in the laboratory?
options: Relative density is a dimensionless ratio relative to a common reference substance (usually water), which simplifies comparisons between different substances without needing to track units explicitly
Relative density offers no practical advantage over measuring absolute density alone
Relative density cannot be meaningfully compared between different substances
Absolute density measurements are always simpler and more generally useful than relative density
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: Relative density is a dimensionless ratio relative to a common reference substance (usually water), which simplifies comparisons between different substances without needing to track units explicitly

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains why an object that neither floats to the surface nor sinks to the bottom of a liquid (i.e., is neutrally buoyant) has an average density equal to that of the surrounding liquid?
options: At neutral buoyancy, the upward Archimedes’ upthrust exactly balances the object’s weight, a condition that occurs specifically when the object’s average density matches that of the surrounding liquid
Neutral buoyancy only occurs when an object’s density is significantly greater than that of the liquid
Neutral buoyancy has no meaningful relationship to how an object’s density compares with the liquid’s density
Neutral buoyancy can only be achieved by an object with zero mass
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: At neutral buoyancy, the upward Archimedes’ upthrust exactly balances the object’s weight, a condition that occurs specifically when the object’s average density matches that of the surrounding liquid

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains how a fish is able to control its depth in water using its internal swim bladder?
options: By adjusting the amount of gas held within its swim bladder, a fish can alter its overall body volume, and hence its average density, allowing it to rise, sink, or remain at a constant depth
A fish’s swim bladder has no meaningful effect on its buoyancy or ability to control its depth
Fish control their depth purely through muscular swimming effort, with no role for buoyancy adjustment
A swim bladder functions only to assist a fish’s breathing, with no relevance to buoyancy control
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: By adjusting the amount of gas held within its swim bladder, a fish can alter its overall body volume, and hence its average density, allowing it to rise, sink, or remain at a constant depth

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a hot-air balloon is able to rise into the air?
options: Heating the air inside the balloon reduces its density below that of the surrounding cooler air, so the resulting upthrust exceeds the combined weight of the balloon, its basket, and the heated air within it
Hot-air balloons rise due to an unrelated chemical reaction, rather than any density difference
Heated air generally has a higher density than the surrounding cooler air
The rising of a hot-air balloon bears no relationship to Archimedes’ principle
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: Heating the air inside the balloon reduces its density below that of the surrounding cooler air, so the resulting upthrust exceeds the combined weight of the balloon, its basket, and the heated air within it

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains why icebergs float with the majority of their volume submerged beneath the water’s surface?
options: Ice has a density only slightly less than that of liquid water, so only a relatively small proportion of an iceberg’s total volume needs to remain above the surface to provide sufficient upthrust to support its full weight
Ice has a much lower density than water, meaning most of an iceberg’s volume typically remains above the surface
Icebergs actually float with their entire volume positioned above the water’s surface
The proportion of an iceberg’s volume above versus below the surface bears no relationship to relative density
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: Ice has a density only slightly less than that of liquid water, so only a relatively small proportion of an iceberg’s total volume needs to remain above the surface to provide sufficient upthrust to support its full weight

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains why accurately determining the density of an irregularly shaped object, such as a small pebble, generally requires the liquid displacement method rather than direct geometric calculation?
options: Irregular shapes lack a straightforward geometric formula for volume calculation, so measuring the volume of liquid displaced provides a practical alternative method for determining the object’s volume and hence its density
Irregularly shaped objects always possess a simple, readily calculable geometric volume
The liquid displacement method cannot be applied to irregularly shaped objects
The density of an irregular object cannot be reliably determined by any practical experimental method
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: Irregular shapes lack a straightforward geometric formula for volume calculation, so measuring the volume of liquid displaced provides a practical alternative method for determining the object’s volume and hence its density

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly explains why sea water is generally somewhat denser than fresh (river or lake) water?
options: The dissolved salts present in sea water add additional mass to a given volume of water, without correspondingly increasing that volume by the same proportion, thereby increasing its overall density
Sea water is always less dense than fresh water, due to its dissolved salt content
Dissolved salt content has no meaningful bearing on a liquid’s overall density
Fresh water and sea water necessarily have identical densities in every case
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: The dissolved salts present in sea water add additional mass to a given volume of water, without correspondingly increasing that volume by the same proportion, thereby increasing its overall density

Liquids at Rest.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of understanding density, upthrust, and Archimedes’ principle, both for natural phenomena and for engineering applications?
options: These concepts explain natural buoyancy-related phenomena, such as floating icebergs and swimming fish, and underpin engineering applications ranging from ship design to submarine operation and the use of hydrometers
Density and Archimedes’ principle bear no meaningful relevance to either natural phenomena or engineering applications
These concepts apply exclusively to abstract, theoretical physics problems, with no genuine real-world relevance
Ship and submarine design require no consideration whatsoever of density or buoyancy-related principles
Liquids at Rest.correct_answer: These concepts explain natural buoyancy-related phenomena, such as floating icebergs and swimming fish, and underpin engineering applications ranging from ship design to submarine operation and the use of hydrometers

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: Temperature is best understood as a measure of
options: the total heat energy contained within a body
the degree of hotness or coldness of a body, related to the average kinetic energy of its particles
the mass of a body
the volume occupied by a body
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: the degree of hotness or coldness of a body, related to the average kinetic energy of its particles

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: A thermometric property is a physical property that
options: stays completely unchanged regardless of temperature
changes measurably and predictably with temperature, making it suitable for constructing a thermometer
bears no relationship to temperature at all
can only be meaningfully observed at absolute zero
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: changes measurably and predictably with temperature, making it suitable for constructing a thermometer

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: Calibrating a thermometer generally involves
options: marking scale divisions arbitrarily, with no reference to any fixed physical condition
establishing fixed reference points, such as the ice point and steam point, and dividing the intervening scale appropriately
disregarding any fixed reference points entirely
relying on a single, arbitrary reference temperature only
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: establishing fixed reference points, such as the ice point and steam point, and dividing the intervening scale appropriately

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: The ice point (lower fixed point) on the Celsius scale corresponds to
options: 0°C, the temperature at which pure ice melts under standard atmospheric pressure
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: 0°C, the temperature at which pure ice melts under standard atmospheric pressure

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: The steam point (upper fixed point) on the Celsius scale corresponds to
options: 100°C, the temperature at which pure water boils under standard atmospheric pressure
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: 100°C, the temperature at which pure water boils under standard atmospheric pressure

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: The Kelvin (absolute) temperature scale places its zero at
options: the ice point (0°C)
absolute zero, approximately -273°C, the theoretical minimum possible temperature
the steam point (100°C)
an arbitrary point unrelated to any physical condition
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: absolute zero, approximately -273°C, the theoretical minimum possible temperature

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: To convert a Celsius temperature to Kelvin, one should generally
options: subtract 273 from the Celsius value
add 273 to the Celsius value
multiply the Celsius value by 273
divide the Celsius value by 273
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: add 273 to the Celsius value

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: A clinical (medical) thermometer is specifically designed to measure
options: very high industrial process temperatures
human body temperature, over a relatively narrow, clinically relevant range
extremely low cryogenic temperatures
atmospheric pressure
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: human body temperature, over a relatively narrow, clinically relevant range

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: A thermocouple thermometer operates based on the principle that
options: a small electromotive force is generated at the junction of two dissimilar metals, varying predictably with temperature
mercury expands and contracts with changes in temperature
it detects colour changes to indicate temperature
it measures atmospheric pressure rather than temperature
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: a small electromotive force is generated at the junction of two dissimilar metals, varying predictably with temperature

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: A resistance thermometer measures temperature based on
options: changes in the electrical resistance of a conductor, typically a metal, with temperature
changes in colour with temperature
changes in the volume of a liquid with temperature
changes in magnetic field strength
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: changes in the electrical resistance of a conductor, typically a metal, with temperature

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: Which of the following correctly explains why mercury, rather than water, is commonly used in traditional liquid-in-glass thermometers?
options: Mercury remains liquid over a wide, practically useful range of temperatures, expands fairly uniformly with temperature, and does not wet the glass
Water actually has a wider useful liquid temperature range than mercury
Mercury freezes at a higher temperature than water, making it generally impractical for most uses
There is no practical advantage to using mercury rather than water for thermometric purposes
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: Mercury remains liquid over a wide, practically useful range of temperatures, expands fairly uniformly with temperature, and does not wet the glass

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a thermocouple thermometer is often preferred for measuring very high or rapidly changing temperatures, compared to a traditional liquid-in-glass thermometer?
options: Thermocouples can respond quickly and can be constructed to withstand and accurately measure much higher temperatures than typical liquid-in-glass designs allow
Thermocouples are always slower to respond than a liquid-in-glass thermometer
Thermocouples are entirely incapable of measuring high temperatures
There is no meaningful practical advantage of thermocouples over liquid-in-glass thermometers for high-temperature measurement
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: Thermocouples can respond quickly and can be constructed to withstand and accurately measure much higher temperatures than typical liquid-in-glass designs allow

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: Converting 30°C to Kelvin gives approximately
Converting 300 K to Celsius gives approximately
Which of the following correctly explains why establishing fixed reference points, such as the ice point and steam point, is essential when constructing a reliable temperature scale?
options: Fixed reference points provide known, reproducible temperature values against which the thermometric property’s scale can be accurately and consistently calibrated
Fixed reference points have no practical role in accurately calibrating a thermometer
A reliable temperature scale can be constructed without reference to any fixed points whatsoever
Any arbitrary, non-reproducible points would work equally well as fixed reference points
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: Fixed reference points provide known, reproducible temperature values against which the thermometric property’s scale can be accurately and consistently calibrated

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the Kelvin scale is generally preferred over the Celsius scale for scientific calculations involving the gas laws?
options: The Kelvin scale begins at absolute zero, giving a direct proportional relationship with quantities such as gas volume and pressure, which would not hold if the Celsius scale (with its arbitrary zero point) were used instead
The Celsius scale is always preferred for scientific gas law calculations
There is no meaningful practical difference between using the Kelvin and Celsius scales for such calculations
The Kelvin scale has an arbitrary, non-physical zero point, similar to the Celsius scale
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: The Kelvin scale begins at absolute zero, giving a direct proportional relationship with quantities such as gas volume and pressure, which would not hold if the Celsius scale (with its arbitrary zero point) were used instead

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a resistance thermometer, despite being more complex than a simple liquid-in-glass thermometer, is often preferred for continuous, automated industrial temperature monitoring?
options: Resistance thermometers can provide precise, easily digitized readings, making them well-suited to continuous, automated monitoring and control systems
Resistance thermometers are always significantly less accurate than a comparable liquid-in-glass thermometer
Industrial monitoring systems generally have no need for precise, automated temperature readings
There is no practical advantage of resistance thermometers over liquid-in-glass designs for industrial monitoring
Temperature and Its Measurement.correct_answer: Resistance thermometers can provide precise, easily digitized readings, making them well-suited to continuous, automated monitoring and control systems

Temperature and Its Measurement.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a clinical thermometer, designed with a narrow temperature range, is preferred over a general-purpose thermometer with a much wider range, for measuring human body temperature?
options: A narrow-range thermometer can provide much finer precision and readability specifically within the range relevant to human body temperature
A narrow-range thermometer is inherently less accurate than a wide-range thermometer
Measuring body temperature requires no particular precision
There is no practical advantage to using a narrow-range thermometer for clinical purposes
